- ATTACK · loudness 570 ms: the volume rises over about 0.6 s when the drone starts, rather than switching on with a click.
- SUSTAIN · loudness 8: with DRONE on, this is the level the drone holds at. It is the volume knob for the drone.
- Listen for: the sound fades in and keeps going with nothing held. For now it is the default bright sawtooth from Oscillator A.

steps.title: Fix Oscillator B on a low C
steps.why:
Oscillator B becomes the pedal note, a low note that stays still whatever you play.
- Osc B triangle only: the softest shape, mostly fundamental. A pedal note should be felt under the line, not buzz over it.
- OCTAVE 0, FREQUENCY 0: the lowest octave, a low C two octaves below middle C, about 65 Hz. Each 0.7 on FREQUENCY is about a semitone if you want another pedal note.
- Osc B keyboard off: the KYBD switch stops B following the keys, so it holds that C. This is what makes it a pedal note. LO FREQ stays on NORMAL so it is still an audio tone.
- OSC B 9, OSC A 0: only the pedal note in the mixer for now.
- Listen for: play several keys. Nothing changes, because the only sound in the mixer ignores the keyboard.

steps.title: Oscillator A is the moving voice
steps.why:
Oscillator A becomes the moving voice above the pedal. It follows the keys, so each note you play sets a new interval against the fixed low C.
- Osc A sawtooth on, pulse off: the brighter shape, so the moving line stands out against the soft triangle below.
- OCTAVE 2, FREQUENCY 0: two octaves above the pedal, in tune with it. SYNC off, so A is free and not locked to B.
- OSC A 6: a little lower than the pedal note at 9, so the bottom stays solid and the saw does not swamp it. NOISE/EXT 0.
- Listen for: play C, then G, then E flat. The low C stays put and the character of the chord changes with each interval.

steps.title: A long glide
steps.why:
Glide (portamento) makes the pitch slide from one note to the next instead of jumping.
- RATE 7 (1.5 s): a long slide. The pitch covers most of the distance in the first second and eases into the new note. Lower settings shorten the slide; at 0 it jumps.
- Glide mode NORMAL: every change of note slides, even if you lift your finger first. AUTO would slide only between overlapping notes.
- Listen for: play two notes far apart. Oscillator A travels slowly between them while the pedal stays still, because Oscillator B is not listening to the keyboard.

steps.title: Dark filter that barely follows the keys
steps.why:
The filter darkens the whole drone and is set so that the pedal note does not change colour as the top voice moves.
- CUTOFF 4.3 (about 390 Hz): low, which takes the edge off the saw and leaves a dark, warm tone. Raise it and the upper voice gets buzzy.
- RESONANCE 1.5: a small boost at the cutoff, a slight focus to the tone.
- ENVELOPE AMOUNT 0: no filter sweep. The gate never closes here, so a sweep would happen only once anyway.
- KEYBOARD AMOUNT 3: the cutoff follows the keys only a little. Higher and the pedal note would brighten every time the upper voice went up.
- Listen for: play high and low notes. The low C keeps nearly the same colour throughout.

steps.title: A slow drift on the cutoff
steps.why:
The LFO (low-frequency oscillator, a slow wave for moving other controls) makes the cutoff drift so the drone never sits completely still.
- LFO triangle on, FREQUENCY 1 (0.14 Hz): a smooth shape at about one cycle every seven seconds. Too slow to hear as a wobble.
- AMOUNT LFO 2: the cutoff moves about a fifth of an octave either way. More and the drift becomes an obvious swell.
- LFO route DIRECT, To FILTER DIR: the LFO goes onto the always-on bus and the filter listens to that bus, so the movement is there without the mod wheel.
- Listen for: hold one note for fifteen seconds. The drone gets slightly brighter and darker in a slow cycle. Set AMOUNT LFO to 0 to hear it go static.

context.mode.drone: Keeps both voices sounding with no key held. Switch it off to stop the drone.
context.oscB.kbd: Off, so Oscillator B ignores the keys and holds one pitch. This is what makes it a pedal note.
context.oscB.freq: Tunes the pedal note. At 0 with OCTAVE at 0 it is a low C; each step of 0.7 on the knob is about a semitone.
context.mix.oscB: The level of the pedal note.
context.mix.oscA: The level of the moving voice.
context.glide.rate: How long Oscillator A takes to reach each new note.
context.filter.kbd: Low, so the brightness of the pedal note stays nearly the same whichever key is down.
context.mod.lfoAmt: How far the cutoff drifts.

tweaks.hear: The pedal note rises five semitones, from C to F, and every interval in the riff changes with it.
At 0 the upper voice steps from note to note like an organ. At 9 it takes several seconds to arrive and spends most of its time between notes.
Oscillator B follows the keys again and the pedal note is gone: the two voices now move together, two octaves apart.
When the upper voice lands on a C it beats slowly against the pedal note.

sounds.name: Soft Keys with Filter Tremolo
sounds.ref: In the style of Portishead — "Roads"
sounds.blurb: Soft, rounded keyboard tone that pulses gently in loudness four or five times a second.
sounds.how: The keyboard on that record is a Fender Rhodes electric piano with tremolo on it. Tremolo is a steady rise and fall in loudness, and the Pro-1 cannot send its LFO to the amplifier. The filter can do the job. The tone here is mostly a triangle wave, which is little more than its lowest harmonic, and the cutoff sits just above that harmonic. When the LFO moves the cutoff down it cuts into the note and the level drops; when it moves up the note comes back. KEYBOARD AMOUNT at 10 keeps the cutoff the same distance above every note, so the tremolo is equally deep across the keyboard.

steps.title: Triangle body, quiet square an octave up
steps.why:
Two oscillators build a soft keyboard tone: a triangle for the body and a square an octave up for a faint bell-like top.
- Osc B triangle only, OCTAVE 2: the triangle is little more than its lowest harmonic, so it is soft and round. This is the body of the note.
- Osc A pulse only, PULSE WIDTH 5 (50 %): a pulse at half width is a square wave, hollow and slightly bright.
- Osc A OCTAVE 3: one octave above the triangle, where it adds a top edge rather than a second note.
- FREQUENCY 0, SYNC off, KYBD on: both in tune and following the keys.
- Listen for: the mixer still has Oscillator A loud and B at 0 at this point, so you mainly hear the square an octave up. The next step fixes the balance.

steps.title: Mostly triangle
steps.why:
The mixer puts the triangle in front and tucks the square underneath.
- OSC B 9: the triangle carries almost all of the note.
- OSC A 3: the square is quiet, just enough to give the note a bell-like top. Turn it up and the tone goes organ-like; to 0 and it goes dull.
- NOISE/EXT 0: no noise.
- Listen for: a round, soft note. Switch OSC A between 0 and 3 to hear the small top it adds.

steps.title: Cutoff just above the note, tracking the keys
steps.why:
The filter is placed just above the note, which is what will let it act as a volume control later.
- CUTOFF 4.2 (about 364 Hz): at middle C that is half an octave above the note. Low enough that moving it cuts into the note itself. Higher settings weaken the tremolo; lower ones make the whole sound faint.
- KEYBOARD AMOUNT 10: the cutoff follows the keys exactly, so it stays the same distance above every note and the effect is equally deep across the keyboard.
- RESONANCE 0.5: almost none, so there is no whistle or peak.
- Listen for: the tone gets darker and a little quieter than before. Play high and low notes: they keep the same colour.

steps.title: A soft knock at the front
steps.why:
The filter envelope (ADSR: attack, decay, sustain, release) gives each note a slightly brighter start that rounds off, like a hammer on a tine.
- ENVELOPE AMOUNT 2: a small lift of the cutoff on each note. More and the knock turns into a synth pluck.
- ATTACK 2 ms: the lift arrives immediately.
- DECAY 270 ms, SUSTAIN 0: the filter falls back over about a quarter of a second and settles at the resting cutoff.
- RELEASE 220 ms: how quickly the filter closes after you let go.
- Listen for: a soft knock at the front of each note, then a rounder tone. Set ENVELOPE AMOUNT to 0 and the knock goes.

steps.title: Volume like a struck instrument
steps.why:
The loudness envelope gives a struck-instrument shape: an immediate start and a slow fade while the key is held.
- ATTACK 3 ms: almost instant, so the note starts cleanly.
- DECAY 2.5 s, SUSTAIN 3: the volume falls slowly over two and a half seconds to a low held level, like a piano note dying away.
- RELEASE 360 ms: a short tail after you let go.
- Retrigger on: RETRIG restarts both envelopes on every key press, so each note gets its own knock even when you play legato.
- Listen for: hold a chord shape note by note and let the sound fade. Play quick repeated notes to hear each one start fresh.

steps.title: Tremolo from the LFO and the filter
steps.why:
The Pro-1 cannot send its LFO (low-frequency oscillator, a slow modulation wave) to the amplifier, so the filter does the job. Moving a cutoff that sits close to the note turns the note up and down.
- LFO triangle on, FREQUENCY 6.8 (4.5 Hz): a smooth wave at about four and a half pulses a second, a relaxed tremolo speed. Faster sounds nervous; slower sounds like a swell.
- AMOUNT LFO 3.5: the cutoff moves about 0.6 of an octave each way. This is the depth of the tremolo.
- LFO route DIRECT, To FILTER DIR: the always-on bus carries the LFO, and the cutoff listens to it. There is no switch for the amplifier.
- Listen for: hold a note. The loudness pulses and the tone gets slightly duller at the bottom of each pulse. Turn AMOUNT LFO to 0 and back to hear it switch off.

context.filter.cutoff: Sits just above the note, so that moving it changes the loudness and not only the tone. Higher settings weaken the tremolo; lower ones make the whole sound faint.
context.filter.kbd: At 10 the cutoff follows the keys exactly, so every note gets the same depth of tremolo.
context.mod.lfoAmt: The depth of the tremolo.
context.lfo.rate: The speed of the tremolo, about 4.5 Hz here.
context.mod.toFilter: Connects the DIRECT bus (carrying the LFO) to the cutoff. There is no switch for the amplifier, which is why the filter does this job.
context.mix.oscA: The quiet square an octave up. It gives the note a bell-like top.
context.aenv.decay: How slowly a held note fades.

tweaks.hear: At 0 the note is steady. At 3.5 it pulses gently. At 5 the note almost disappears at the bottom of each pulse.

tweaks.try: Flip to WHEEL and set the FILTER switch to WH
tweaks.hear: The tremolo is off until you push the mod wheel, and the wheel sets its depth. Bring it in on long notes only.
The cutoff is now well clear of the note, so the tremolo nearly vanishes and only the square on top flickers.

tweaks.try: Switch triangle off and pulse on
tweaks.hear: The loudness now switches between two levels instead of swelling, which is how some electric-piano tremolos sound at full depth.

sounds.name: Soft Triangle Pluck with a Noise Tick
sounds.ref: In the style of Depeche Mode — "Any Second Now (Voices)"
sounds.blurb: Small, clear pluck with a soft tick at the front, close to a thumb piano.
sounds.how: Oscillator A is not used at all. The note is Oscillator B’s triangle, a smooth tone with almost no buzz, and the volume envelope makes it die away in about half a second. A triangle alone has no front edge, so a little noise is mixed in to give one. The filter envelope opens the filter wide for less than a tenth of a second, which lets the noise through as a tick, and then closes it to about an octave above the note. From then on the triangle passes almost untouched and nearly all of the noise is removed.

steps.title: Oscillator B’s triangle alone
steps.why:
The whole pitched part of the sound is one triangle wave. A triangle is smooth, with almost no buzz, so later the filter can shape the noise without changing the note.
- Osc B triangle only: soft and pure. Saw and pulse off.
- OCTAVE 3: the highest octave, so the notes sit high like a thumb piano.
- FREQUENCY 0, LO FREQ on NORMAL, KYBD on: in tune and following the keys.
- OSC A 0, OSC B 8: Oscillator A is not part of this sound, and B takes its place in the mixer.
- Listen for: a clear, flute-like tone with no front edge. Held notes stay at full level for now.

steps.title: A short, fading note
steps.why:
The loudness envelope turns the held tone into a short pluck that dies away by itself.
- ATTACK 2 ms: instant start.
- DECAY 550 ms, SUSTAIN 0: the volume falls to nothing over about half a second, even if you keep the key down. This is the length of the note. Longer decay rings on; shorter becomes a blip.
- RELEASE 360 ms: if you let go before the decay ends, the note finishes over about a third of a second.
- Retrigger on: RETRIG gives every key press a fresh start, so fast repeated notes all pluck.
- Listen for: short fading notes. Something is still missing at the front: the triangle alone starts softly.

steps.title: Add noise
steps.why:
Noise is added as the material for the tick. For now it is too much.
- NOISE/EXT 7: white noise, a hiss with energy at all frequencies, mixed in well up. More noise will give a harder front later.
- Listen for: with the filter still wide open you hear hiss through the whole note, fading with it. The next two steps turn that hiss into a short tick.

steps.title: Close the filter to just above the note
steps.why:
The filter closes to just above the note, so the triangle passes and most of the noise is removed.
- CUTOFF 5.6 (about 960 Hz): the resting position. It decides how much noise is left under the note after the tick. Higher lets more hiss through.
- KEYBOARD AMOUNT 8: the cutoff follows the keys closely, so it stays about an octave above whichever note you play.
- RESONANCE 0.5: almost none, so no whistle.
- Listen for: the hiss drops away to a faint shadow and the triangle comes through nearly untouched. Now the front of the note is soft again.

steps.title: Open it for a moment at the start
steps.why:
The filter envelope (ADSR: attack, decay, sustain, release) opens the filter for a moment at the start of each note, letting the noise through as a tick.
- ENVELOPE AMOUNT 5.5: the filter opens by more than four octaves at the peak. More gives a brighter, harder tick.
- ATTACK 2 ms: the filter opens at once.
- DECAY 85 ms, SUSTAIN 0: it falls straight back to the resting cutoff. At 85 ms the tick is a tap; longer turns it into a puff of breath.
- RELEASE 110 ms: the filter closes quickly after you let go.
- Listen for: a soft tick on the front of each note, close to a thumb piano. Sweep DECAY between 3 and 6 while playing to hear the tap turn into a breath.

context.mix.oscA: At 0: Oscillator A is not part of this sound.
context.oscB.tri: The whole pitched part of the sound. A triangle is smooth enough that the filter hardly changes it.
context.mix.noise: The material for the tick. More noise gives a harder front.
context.filter.cutoff: The resting position, about an octave above the note. It decides how much noise is left under the note after the tick.
context.filter.env: How far the filter opens for the tick.
context.fenv.decay: The length of the tick. At 85 ms it is a tap; longer and it becomes a puff of breath.
context.aenv.decay: The length of the note.

tweaks.hear: At 0 the note has no front at all, like a soft beep. At 7 it has a small tap, as if something struck it.
The tick stretches into a breathy "chiff", closer to a blown pipe than a plucked one.
An octave lower the pluck is rounder and closer to a marimba.
Notes ring for about two seconds and start to overlap the next one in the riff.

sounds.name: Slow Surf from Noise
sounds.ref: In the style of Jean-Michel Jarre — "Oxygène (Part VI)"
sounds.blurb: Waves of filtered noise that lie quiet for several seconds, wash in and draw back, with no key held.
sounds.how: There is no oscillator in this sound: only noise goes into the filter, and DRONE keeps it running. The LFO moves the cutoff, so each rise of the LFO is a wave that gets brighter and louder. An ordinary LFO would make every wave rise and fall evenly, which sounds mechanical. A cable from LFO OUT back into LFO CV lets the LFO control its own speed: it crawls while it is low and hurries while it is high. The sound stays low and quiet for most of each cycle, and the wave itself comes and goes in a second or two.

steps.title: Hold the gate open
steps.why:
DRONE holds the gate open, so the sound runs by itself with no key held. The gate is the on signal that starts the envelopes.
- Drone on: the envelopes rise to their sustain level and stay there. Switch it off to stop the sea.
- Repeat off: the envelopes are not re-fired, so the sound is continuous.
- ATTACK · loudness 260 ms: a gentle fade in when the drone starts.
- SUSTAIN · loudness 7: with DRONE on, this is the level the sound holds at.
- Listen for: the default sawtooth comes on and stays on without a key. The next step swaps it for noise.

steps.title: Noise only
steps.why:
Only noise goes into the filter. There is no oscillator in this sound at all.
- OSC A 0, OSC B 0: both oscillators out of the mixer.
- NOISE/EXT 10: white noise at full level. It is the only sound source.
- VOLUME 10: filtered noise is quieter than an oscillator, so the master output goes up. Turn it back to 7 before you bring an oscillator into the mixer again.
- Listen for: a steady hiss, like a radio between stations. The filter steps give it shape.

steps.title: The middle of the movement
steps.why:
The filter sets the centre that the waves will move around.
- CUTOFF 6.2 (about 1.4 kHz): the middle of the movement. For now the noise is brighter than it will be between waves. Lower settings make the quiet stretch darker and the waves duller, as if heard from further away.
- RESONANCE 2: a little boost at the cutoff gives the noise a faint hollow pitch, which helps it sound like water. Too much and the waves start to whistle.
- ENVELOPE AMOUNT 0: no sweep from the filter envelope; the gate never closes anyway.
- KEYBOARD AMOUNT 4: the key you press shifts the whole sound a little brighter or darker.
- Listen for: a softer, slightly hollow hiss. Press a high key and a low key to hear the colour shift.

steps.title: Let the LFO move the cutoff
steps.why:
The LFO (low-frequency oscillator, a slow wave used to move other controls) moves the cutoff up and down, and the noise gets louder as it gets brighter.
- LFO triangle on, FREQUENCY 1.8 (0.23 Hz): an even up-and-down shape, once every four seconds.
- AMOUNT LFO 7: the cutoff moves about two and a half octaves each way. This sets the size of each wave.
- LFO route DIRECT, To FILTER DIR: the always-on bus carries the LFO and the filter listens to it.
- Listen for: the hiss rising and falling in a steady cycle. It works, but the quiet part is as short as the loud part, so it sounds more like breathing than like the sea.

steps.title: Patch LFO OUT into LFO CV
steps.why:
A cable lets the LFO control its own speed, so each cycle crawls through the quiet part and hurries through the wave.
- LFO OUT to LFO CV: click LFO OUT, then LFO CV. LFO OUT sends the LFO wave as a voltage; LFO CV (control voltage) is the input that adds to the speed knob. While the wave is low it slows the LFO by up to three octaves; while it is high it speeds it up by the same.
- FREQUENCY · lfo rate: still sets the overall pace. There is no depth control on the jack.
- Listen for: one cycle now takes about eight seconds, and nearly all of it is spent in a long, low rumble. Then a wave arrives and leaves within a second or two. Pull the cable out and back to compare with the even breathing of the step before.

context.mode.drone: Keeps the sea running with no key held. Switch it off to stop it.
context.out.volume: At 10 because filtered noise is quiet. Turn it back to 7 before you bring any oscillator up in the mixer.
context.filter.cutoff: The centre of the movement. Lower settings make the quiet stretch darker and the waves duller, as if heard from further away.
context.filter.res: Gives the noise a faint pitch. Too much and the waves start to whistle.
context.mod.lfoAmt: The size of each wave: how much brighter and louder the noise gets at the top.
context.lfo.rate: The overall pace. With the cable in, the quiet part of each cycle is far longer than the wave.
context.filter.kbd: Lets the key you press shift the whole sound a little brighter or darker.

tweaks.hear: At 1 a wave comes about every thirteen seconds. At 3 they come every four seconds.
Smaller, more distant waves.
The noise narrows into a pitched whoosh, closer to wind round a building than to water.

tweaks.try: Switch triangle off and sawtooth on
tweaks.hear: Each wave builds slowly and then cuts off at once, because the ramp drops straight back to the bottom.

sounds.name: Self-Playing Sine Tones
sounds.ref: In the style of Brian Eno — "Neroli"
sounds.blurb: Soft, pure tones that sound one at a time every few seconds, in a pattern of high and low that does not settle.
sounds.how: All three mixer levels are at 0. With RESONANCE at 10 the filter oscillates by itself and gives a sine-like tone at its cutoff frequency, and KEYBOARD AMOUNT at 10 lets the keys tune it. REPEAT makes the slow LFO fire the volume envelope about once every three seconds while a key is held, so one held key gives a slow row of fading tones. Oscillator B is switched to LO FREQ and taken off the keyboard, and its pulse wave moves the cutoff between two positions a fifth apart. It runs at a speed that has nothing to do with the LFO, so which of the two pitches each tone gets, and whether it changes part-way through, keeps shifting.

steps.title: Let the filter be the voice
steps.why:
The filter becomes the sound source. At full resonance it oscillates by itself and gives a pure, sine-like tone at the cutoff frequency.
- OSC A 0, OSC B 0, NOISE/EXT 0: nothing goes into the filter. Every sound from here on comes from the filter itself.
- RESONANCE 10: resonance boosts the cutoff point; at maximum the boost is enough to make the filter whistle on its own.
- KEYBOARD AMOUNT 10: the cutoff follows the keys exactly, so the keys play the filter in tune.
- CUTOFF 4.7 (about 514 Hz): now the tuning knob. Middle C gives about 510 Hz. Turn it and the whole pitch moves.
- ENVELOPE AMOUNT 0: no sweep, so the pitch stays steady.
- Listen for: hold a key and you hear a pure tone. Play up the keyboard to check it follows.

steps.title: Shape one soft tone
steps.why:
The loudness envelope (ADSR: attack, decay, sustain, release) turns the steady whistle into one soft tone that fades.
- ATTACK 23 ms: just enough to take the click off the start.
- DECAY 1.8 s, SUSTAIN 0: with no sustain, the tone fades away slowly for as long as the gate is open. Longer decay rings on; shorter makes a blip.
- RELEASE 570 ms: finishes the fade after the gate closes.
- VOLUME 10: a self-oscillating filter is quieter than the oscillators. Turn it back to 7 before bringing any oscillator into the mixer.
- Listen for: each key press gives one tone that dies away over a couple of seconds.

steps.title: REPEAT at a slow LFO rate
steps.why:
REPEAT makes the LFO (low-frequency oscillator, here a slow clock) fire the envelopes again and again while a key is held.
- Repeat on: while a key is down, the LFO opens the gate for the first half of each cycle and closes it for the second.
- Drone off: the gate is not held open, so REPEAT can open and close it.
- FREQUENCY · lfo rate 2.5 (0.35 Hz): one cycle every 2.8 seconds. This is the gap between tones. Faster packs the tones together; slower leaves long silences.
- Listen for: hold one key and wait. A tone, a fade, a silence, another tone, all at the same pitch for now.

steps.title: Turn Oscillator B into a slow switch
steps.why:
Oscillator B is turned into a slow switch that will move the pitch between two positions. It makes no sound, because its mixer level is 0.
- Osc B low frequency LO FREQ: drops B far below hearing so it works as a second LFO.
- Osc B keyboard off: B ignores the keys, so its speed does not change with the note.
- Osc B pulse only, PULSE WIDTH 5 (50 %): a square jumps between two values and spends half its time on each.
- OCTAVE 0, FREQUENCY −3.4: in LO FREQ these set the speed, here about one flip a second. Small changes give a different pattern.
- Listen for: nothing yet. The switch is running but not connected to anything.

steps.title: Send it to the filter
steps.why:
Oscillator B’s slow square is sent to the filter, so each tone lands on one of two pitches a fifth apart.
- AMOUNT OSC B 2.4: sets the distance between the two pitches. The cutoff, and so the pitch, jumps about three and a half semitones up or down from where the key put it: a fifth apart in all. More amount widens the leap.
- OSC B route DIRECT: B goes onto the always-on bus.
- To FILTER DIR: the cutoff listens to the DIRECT bus.
- Listen for: hold one key for half a minute. Some tones are high, some are low, and some step from one pitch to the other as they fade. B runs at a speed unrelated to the LFO, so the pattern keeps shifting. Nudge Osc B FREQUENCY to change it.

context.filter.res: At 10 the filter oscillates by itself. This is the only sound source.
context.filter.cutoff: The tuning knob for the tones.
context.filter.kbd: At 10 the cutoff follows the keys exactly, so the key you hold sets the pitch the two tones sit around.
context.mode.repeat: Lets the LFO fire the envelopes again and again while a key is held.
context.lfo.rate: The gap between tones.
context.oscB.freq: In LO FREQ this is the speed of the high-low switch. Small changes give a different pattern.
context.oscB.pw: The share of time spent on the high pitch. At 5 it is half and half.
context.mod.oscBAmt: The distance between the two pitches. At 2.4 it is about a fifth.
context.aenv.decay: How long each tone takes to fade.
context.out.volume: At 10 because the filter alone is quiet. Turn it back to 7 before you bring any oscillator up in the mixer.

tweaks.hear: The order of high and low tones changes. Near −2 Oscillator B flips more than once a second, so most tones step between the two pitches as they fade.

tweaks.try: Switch pulse off and triangle on
tweaks.hear: The pitch no longer jumps. Each tone lands somewhere between the two pitches and slides a little as it fades.
The two pitches move apart to about an octave.

tweaks.try: Set to 1 with the filter ATTACK at 4 and SUSTAIN at 10
tweaks.hear: Each tone bends upwards at the start, which turns it into a drop of water.

sounds.name: Quiet Arpeggio with Blooming Long Notes
sounds.ref: In the style of New Order — "Your Silent Face"
sounds.blurb: Soft, muted broken-chord pattern in which the long notes open up and the short ones stay dull.
sounds.how: A pulse wave with a quiet saw an octave below goes through a filter that is nearly closed. The filter envelope has a slow attack of about half a second. A short note in the pattern ends before the envelope has got far, so it stays dull. A long note gives the envelope time to reach its peak, so it opens into a clearer tone. Note length becomes the accent, with no change in loudness. The LFO at its slowest also moves the cutoff a little, so the pattern drifts between darker and clearer over twelve seconds.

steps.title: Pulse wave over a quiet low saw
steps.why:
A pulse wave with a quiet saw an octave below gives a soft, slightly hollow tone for a broken-chord pattern.
- Osc A pulse only, PULSE WIDTH 4 (41 %): a little narrower than a square, so slightly thinner and more nasal than a hollow square.
- Osc A OCTAVE 2, FREQUENCY 0, SYNC off: the main voice, in tune.
- Osc B sawtooth, OCTAVE 1: an octave below A, adding warmth underneath. FREQUENCY +0.1 puts it slightly sharp, so the two move against each other a little.
- OSC A 7, OSC B 4, NOISE/EXT 0: the pulse leads and the saw sits low in the mix.
- Listen for: with the filter still open the tone is bright and buzzy for now. Mute OSC B to hear how much weight it adds.

steps.title: Nearly closed filter
steps.why:
The filter is nearly closed, so the resting tone is muted and dull.
- CUTOFF 3.8 (about 280 Hz): low. Most of the edge is gone. This is the dull tone the short notes will keep.
- RESONANCE 2.5: a little boost at the cutoff, so when the filter opens later it has some focus.
- KEYBOARD AMOUNT 7: the cutoff follows the keys most of the way, so the top notes of the pattern are not swallowed.
- Listen for: a muffled, soft pattern. Play the riff and compare high and low notes: they sound similarly muted.

steps.title: A filter envelope slower than the short notes
steps.why:
The filter envelope (ADSR: attack, decay, sustain, release) is slower than the short notes, so note length decides how bright a note gets.
- ENVELOPE AMOUNT 5: how far a long note opens.
- ATTACK 490 ms: the filter takes about half a second to reach its peak. The short notes in the riff last about 180 ms and end long before; the long ones last about 680 ms and get there.
- DECAY 420 ms, SUSTAIN 4: after the peak the filter eases back to a middle level while the note is held.
- RELEASE 360 ms: how fast it closes after the key comes up.
- Listen for: play the riff. The short notes barely open and the long ones bloom into a clearer tone. The accent comes from length, not from loudness.

steps.title: Soft start, ringing tail
steps.why:
The loudness envelope gives each note a soft start and a tail that rings under the next.
- ATTACK 15 ms: removes the click without making the notes late.
- DECAY 420 ms, SUSTAIN 8: a slight fall after the start to a steady held level.
- RELEASE 570 ms: about 0.6 s of tail after each note, so notes ring into each other.
- Retrigger on: RETRIG restarts both envelopes on every note, so each one blooms from the bottom even when notes overlap.
- Listen for: the pattern gains a soft, joined feel. Switch Retrigger off and the overlapping notes stop blooming.

steps.title: A very slow drift
steps.why:
The LFO (low-frequency oscillator, a slow modulation wave) makes the whole pattern drift between darker and clearer.
- LFO triangle on, FREQUENCY 0 (0.08 Hz): a smooth shape at its slowest, one cycle every twelve seconds.
- AMOUNT LFO 2.5: moves the cutoff about a third of an octave each way. More and the drift becomes an obvious sweep.
- LFO route DIRECT, To FILTER DIR: the LFO goes onto the always-on bus and the cutoff listens to it.
- Listen for: loop the riff for half a minute. The whole pattern gets a little clearer and then a little darker again.

context.fenv.attack: Slower than the short notes and quicker than the long ones. This is what makes note length work as an accent.
context.filter.env: How far a long note opens.
context.filter.cutoff: The dull tone of the short notes.
context.filter.kbd: Keeps the higher notes of the pattern from being duller than the low ones.
context.aenv.release: The tail that lets each note ring under the next.
context.mod.lfoAmt: How far the slow drift moves the cutoff, about a third of an octave each way.
context.mode.retrig: Restarts both envelopes on every note, so each one blooms from the bottom.

tweaks.hear: At 0 every note opens at once and the pattern is evenly bright. At 6.8 only the long notes open. At 8.5 even the long notes stay muted.
The long notes open much further and stand out clearly from the rest.
The slow drift becomes a clear rise and fall in brightness over several bars.
A thinner, more nasal pattern, closer to a plucked string.

sounds.name: One-Oscillator Ensemble Strings
sounds.ref: In the style of Joy Division — "Atmosphere"
sounds.blurb: Soft, slowly shifting string tone from a single oscillator, moved by two modulators at different speeds.
sounds.how: The strings on that record came from a string machine. Instruments of that kind get their ensemble sound from a chorus circuit driven by two LFOs at once, one slow and one fast. The Pro-1 can copy that idea with pulse width. Oscillator A has sawtooth and pulse switched on together. Oscillator B goes to LO FREQ as a slow second LFO, and both it and the main LFO are routed to the DIRECT bus. OSC A PW listens to that bus, so the pulse width gets a slow, wide movement with a faster, smaller one on top. The cost is that only one oscillator is left to make sound.

steps.title: Saw and pulse together on Oscillator A
steps.why:
One oscillator is set up with two waveforms at once: a saw for a steady body and a pulse that will be moved later.
- Osc A sawtooth and pulse on: on the Pro-1 each shape has its own switch and they add together. The saw is not affected by pulse width, so it keeps the tone full when the pulse gets narrow.
- PULSE WIDTH 5 (50 %): the pulse starts as a square. This is the part that will move.
- OCTAVE 2, FREQUENCY 0, SYNC off: a plain, in-tune oscillator.
- OSC A 8, OSC B 0, NOISE/EXT 0: only Oscillator A in the mixer.
- Listen for: a bright, static organ-like tone for now.

steps.title: Slow movement from Oscillator B
steps.why:
Oscillator B becomes a slow second LFO (low-frequency oscillator) and moves Oscillator A’s pulse width. Moving pulse width (PWM, pulse width modulation) gives a shifting, chorus-like tone.
- Osc B LO FREQ, keyboard off: B drops below hearing and ignores the keys. It makes no sound here.
- Osc B triangle only: the smoothest modulation shape.
- OCTAVE 0, FREQUENCY −2.9: in LO FREQ these set the speed, about 0.6 Hz.
- AMOUNT OSC B 5.5, route DIRECT: the depth of the slow movement, on the always-on bus.
- To OSC A PW DIR: A’s pulse width listens to that bus. It now swings slowly between about 36 % and 64 %.
- Listen for: hold a note. The tone slowly thickens and thins, like a string section moving.

steps.title: Faster, smaller movement from the LFO
steps.why:
The main LFO adds a faster, smaller movement on the same bus, as a string machine’s chorus uses a slow and a fast modulator together.
- LFO triangle on, FREQUENCY 7.1 (5.4 Hz): a smooth wave at about five cycles a second.
- AMOUNT LFO 2.5: the depth of the fast movement. Keep it well below the slow one or it turns into a buzz.
- LFO route DIRECT: it joins Oscillator B on the DIRECT bus, so OSC A PW gets both mixed together.
- Listen for: alone this is a fine flutter; on top of the slow swing it breaks up the regular rise and fall. Set AMOUNT LFO to 0 and back to hear the ensemble collapse to a simple sweep.

steps.title: Mellow filter
steps.why:
The filter takes the fizz off the top and adds a slight brightening after each note starts.
- CUTOFF 5.6 (about 960 Hz): mellow, a little under 1 kHz. Higher and the strings get harsh.
- RESONANCE 0.5: almost none, so no peak.
- KEYBOARD AMOUNT 6: higher notes open the filter more than halfway, so the top of a chord keeps its air.
- ENVELOPE AMOUNT 1.5, slow filter ADSR: the filter envelope (ADSR: attack, decay, sustain, release) lifts the cutoff slightly on each note. ATTACK 380 ms makes it slow; DECAY 660 ms, SUSTAIN 7 and RELEASE 920 ms keep it smooth.
- Listen for: notes start slightly darker and brighten a little over the first half second.

steps.title: Fade in, fade out
steps.why:
The loudness envelope gives strings their fade in and fade out. This is what makes it strings and not an organ.
- ATTACK 260 ms: each note fades in over about a quarter of a second.
- DECAY 420 ms, SUSTAIN 9: a slight dip after the attack to a nearly full held level.
- RELEASE 920 ms: nearly a second of fade after you let go, so chords join.
- Listen for: soft entries and tails. Set ATTACK to 0 to hear it turn back into an organ.

context.oscA.saw: On together with the pulse. It is not affected by pulse width, so it keeps the tone full when the pulse gets narrow.
context.oscB.lo: Turns Oscillator B into a second LFO. It makes no sound here.
context.oscB.freq: In LO FREQ this is the speed of the slow movement, about 0.6 Hz here.
context.mod.oscBAmt: The depth of the slow movement.
context.mod.lfoAmt: The depth of the fast movement. Keep it well below the slow one or it turns into a buzz.
context.lfo.rate: The speed of the fast movement, about 5.4 Hz here.
context.mod.toAPw: Listens to the DIRECT bus, which carries both modulators mixed together.
context.aenv.attack: The fade-in that makes this strings and not an organ.

tweaks.hear: At 0 you hear one slow, regular sweep. At 2.5 the sweep is broken up and sounds more like several players.
Without the slow movement the fast one is left alone: a thin, nervous flutter.
Only the moving pulse is left. The effect is stronger and the tone is thinner and more hollow.
The slow movement runs from one cycle every two and a half seconds to about one a second.

sounds.name: Tenor Saxophone Line
sounds.ref: In the style of a tenor saxophone solo line
sounds.blurb: Reedy tenor-register solo voice with a resonant middle and a growl on the mod wheel.
sounds.how: A saxophone is a reed and a cone, so the tone is a full harmonic spread with a strong peak in the middle of the range. Oscillator A supplies the sawtooth, Oscillator B a narrow pulse tuned a hair sharp against it, and a trace of noise sits in the body of the note. Resonance at 4.5 puts the peak in. The note shape is built to be blown rather than struck: a 22 ms attack, sustain at full, and a release of about 90 ms so the line stops when you stop. Oscillator B is also wired to the filter through the WHEEL bus, so pushing the mod wheel part-way through a held note adds the rasp a player gets by growling into the horn.

steps.title: Saw plus a narrow pulse
steps.why:
Two oscillators build a reedy tone: a full saw with a thin pulse under it, tuned a hair apart so the pair beat slowly. That slow beating stops it sounding like one static oscillator.
- Osc A sawtooth only: every harmonic, the full spread a sax has.
- Osc B pulse only, PULSE WIDTH 3.5 (36 %): narrower than a square, so thin and nasal on its own. Nearer 5 it goes hollow and clarinet-like; nearer 2 it gets thin and buzzy.
- OCTAVE 2 on both, SYNC off: the same register, both free-running.
- Osc B FREQUENCY +0.2: B a fraction of a semitone sharp. This is where the slow movement inside a held note comes from.
- LO FREQ NORMAL, KYBD on: B is an ordinary oscillator following the keys.
- Listen for: with the mixer still at its start point you hear mainly Oscillator A. The next step brings B in.

steps.title: A little noise in the body
steps.why:
The mixer sets the balance of the two oscillators and puts a little air inside the note.
- OSC A 7.5, OSC B 6: the saw leads and the pulse sits just under it, adding the nasal edge.
- NOISE/EXT 1.5: a quiet hiss inside the note, like breath through the reed. Past about 3 it starts to sound like a fault rather than air.
- Listen for: turn NOISE/EXT to 0 and back. At 0 the tone is clean and synthetic; at 1.5 it has some air in it. Mute OSC B to hear the slow beating disappear.

steps.title: Resonant peak in the middle
steps.why:
The filter puts a resonant peak in the middle of the tone, the band a sax body rings at. Without it the sound is a plain filtered saw.
- CUTOFF 5.2 (about 730 Hz): removes the fizz and places the peak in the mid range.
- RESONANCE 4.5: a clear boost at the cutoff. That peak is what makes the sound read as a reed; at 0 it is a plain saw.
- ENVELOPE AMOUNT 2.5: how far the filter envelope lifts the cutoff at the start of each note (shaped in the next step).
- KEYBOARD AMOUNT 8: moves the peak with the note, so the top of the line does not go dull.
- Listen for: a honky, vocal middle to the tone. Sweep CUTOFF slowly and hear the peak move through the sound.

steps.title: A small push at the front
steps.why:
The filter envelope (ADSR: attack, decay, sustain, release) gives each note a small push at the front, the sound of the reed starting to speak rather than a percussive click.
- ATTACK 10 ms: the lift arrives quickly but not instantly.
- DECAY 170 ms, SUSTAIN 5: the filter eases back to a middle level while the note is held. With ENVELOPE AMOUNT at 2.5, the peak is about two octaves above the resting cutoff.
- RELEASE 87 ms: the filter closes quickly after you let go.
- Listen for: a slightly brighter start to each note that settles. Set ENVELOPE AMOUNT to 0 to hear the notes go flat and lifeless.

steps.title: Blown, not struck
steps.why:
The loudness envelope makes the note blown, not struck: it arrives a moment late, holds, and stops when you stop.
- ATTACK 23 ms: about 22 ms, so the reed takes a moment to speak. At 0 the notes would click.
- DECAY 170 ms, SUSTAIN 10: full sustain, so a held note does not fade under your finger.
- RELEASE 87 ms: about 90 ms, short, so the line stops when you stop playing.
- Listen for: play the riff. Notes start softly but promptly and end cleanly.

steps.title: Slur the overlapping notes
steps.why:
Glide makes the pitch slide between notes. Here it is short and only on the joined notes, like a player slurring.
- RATE 1.5 (68 ms): a slide of about 70 ms, short enough to read as a joined note rather than a swoop.
- Glide mode AUTO: AUTO slides only when you press a new key while still holding the last one (legato), so you choose which notes slur.
- Retrigger off: with RETRIG off, a slurred note changes pitch without restarting the envelopes.
- Listen for: in the riff the overlapping notes glide into each other with no new attack; the detached ones start fresh.

steps.title: Growl on the mod wheel
steps.why:
Oscillator B, already in the mixer, is also used as a modulator for the filter, but only on the mod wheel. At audio rate it shakes the cutoff hundreds of times a second, which you hear as a rasp rather than a wobble.
- AMOUNT OSC B 6: the most growl the wheel can reach.
- OSC B route WHEEL: B goes onto the WHEEL bus, which is scaled by the mod wheel. With the wheel down nothing changes.
- To FILTER WH: the cutoff listens to the WHEEL bus (switch up).
- Listen for: hold a long note and push the wheel halfway through. The note roughens into a growl, like a player growling into the horn.

context.oscB.pw: The narrow pulse. Nearer 5 the tone gets hollow and clarinet-like; nearer 2 it gets thin and buzzy.
context.oscB.freq: A fifth of a semitone sharp. This is where the slow movement inside a held note comes from.
context.mix.noise: The hiss inside the note. Past about 3 it starts to sound like a fault rather than air.
context.filter.res: The peak that makes this a reed. At 0 the sound is a plain filtered saw.
context.filter.kbd: Keeps the tone even from the bottom of the line to the top.
context.aenv.attack: About 22 ms. The reed takes a moment to speak; at 0 the notes would click.
context.aenv.sustain: At 10, so a held note does not fade under your finger.
context.aenv.release: Short, so the line stops when you stop playing.
context.glide.mode: AUTO, so only the overlapping notes in the riff slide.
context.mode.retrig: Off, so a slurred note changes pitch without starting again.
context.mod.oscBAmt: The most growl the wheel can reach. Oscillator B is doing two jobs here: it is in the mixer and it is a modulator.
context.mod.toFilter: Up (WH) listens to the WHEEL bus, so the growl is only there while you push the wheel.

tweaks.try: Set to 8, hold a low note and push the wheel slowly
tweaks.hear: A clean note that tears into a rasp and back again, under your left hand.
At 2 the tone is flat and saw-like. At 7 the peak is so strong the note starts to honk.
The nasal edge goes and the voice drops back to a plain saw.
From a hard tongued start to a note that eases in over about 75 ms.

sounds.name: Open Trumpet Line
sounds.ref: In the style of an open trumpet solo line
sounds.blurb: Bright sawtooth solo voice whose tone blooms open over the first tenth of a second of every note.
sounds.how: The thing that marks a trumpet out is not its waveform but its front edge: the tone arrives a moment after the note and keeps brightening for about a tenth of a second as the lip settles. Two sawtooths, barely detuned, give the harmonic spread. The filter starts low and the filter envelope has a slow attack rather than an instant one, so the brightness grows in instead of snapping. KEYBOARD AMOUNT at 8.5 makes the high notes of the line brighter than the low ones, which is what a trumpet does as it climbs. Vibrato is on the mod wheel, because a player adds it late in a long note, not at the start.

steps.title: Two sawtooths, barely apart
steps.why:
Two sawtooths barely apart give a trumpet its full, bright harmonic spread.
- Osc A and B sawtooth only: every harmonic, the bright raw material a brass sound needs.
- OCTAVE 2 on both, SYNC off: the same register, both free.
- Osc B FREQUENCY +0.1: B about a seventh of a semitone sharp. At 0 the saws lock together and the tone goes flat and static; any more and it sounds like two instruments.
- LO FREQ NORMAL, KYBD on: B plays as a normal oscillator.
- Listen for: B is still at 0 in the mixer, so this sounds like one bright saw for now.

steps.title: One voice in front, one behind
steps.why:
The mixer puts one voice in front and one behind.
- OSC A 8: carries the note.
- OSC B 5: thickens it. Keep B the quieter of the two or the detuning becomes obvious.
- NOISE/EXT 0: no noise.
- Listen for: a slightly wider, moving tone. Turn OSC B up to 8 to hear the detune become too obvious.

steps.title: Start the filter low
steps.why:
The filter starts each note far darker than it ends up. The envelope will do the rest.
- CUTOFF 4.2 (about 364 Hz): the dark starting point. Raise it and the bloom has less distance to travel, so the front edge gets weaker.
- RESONANCE 2.5: a little boost at the cutoff, which sharpens the moment the tone opens.
- ENVELOPE AMOUNT 5: about four octaves of travel for the filter envelope.
- KEYBOARD AMOUNT 8.5: lifts the cutoff as the line rises, so the high notes are brighter than the low ones, as a trumpet is when it climbs.
- Listen for: the envelope is still at its default, so notes open quickly and fall back. The next step slows the opening.

steps.title: Bloom it open, do not snap it
steps.why:
The filter envelope (ADSR: attack, decay, sustain, release) is the whole sound here. A trumpet’s tone arrives a moment after the note and keeps brightening as the lip settles.
- ATTACK 97 ms: the four octaves of travel are spread over about 100 ms instead of arriving at once. This separates a trumpet from a synth stab.
- DECAY 420 ms, SUSTAIN 5.5: after the bloom, the tone eases back to how bright the note stays while held.
- RELEASE 87 ms: the filter closes quickly when you let go.
- Listen for: the first moment of a long note. The pitch is there before the brightness is. Set ATTACK to 0 and the bloom turns into a snap.

steps.title: Blown volume shape
steps.why:
The loudness envelope gives a blown shape: a quick but soft start, full level while held, and a clean stop.
- ATTACK 15 ms: fast enough to play lines, soft enough not to click.
- DECAY 170 ms, SUSTAIN 10: full sustain, so held notes keep their level.
- RELEASE 72 ms: about 70 ms, so a line stops when the player stops.
- Listen for: clean gaps between detached notes in the riff.

steps.title: Slur the joins
steps.why:
Glide slurs the joins between notes, as a player does without re-tonguing.
- RATE 1.2 (43 ms): a slide of about 45 ms, a join rather than a swoop.
- Glide mode AUTO: AUTO slides only when a new key goes down while the last is still held.
- Retrigger off: slurred notes do not restart the envelopes, so only detached notes get a fresh bloom.
- Listen for: the overlapping notes in the riff join up; the separate ones each bloom open again.

steps.title: Vibrato on the mod wheel
steps.why:
The LFO (low-frequency oscillator, a slow wave used to move other controls) adds vibrato, but only on the mod wheel, because a player adds it late in a long note.
- LFO triangle on, FREQUENCY 7.2 (5.7 Hz): a smooth wave at a natural vibrato speed.
- AMOUNT LFO 1.5: the widest vibrato the wheel can reach, about half a semitone each way.
- LFO route WHEEL: the LFO goes onto the WHEEL bus, so it arrives only as you push the wheel.
- To OSC A FREQ WH, To OSC B FREQ WH: both oscillators’ pitch listen to the WHEEL bus, so they move together and stay in tune with each other.
- Listen for: hold a long note, then push the wheel in the second half of it.

context.oscB.freq: A very small detune. At 0 the two saws lock together and the tone goes flat and static.
context.filter.cutoff: Where each note starts. Raise it and the bloom has less distance to travel, so the front edge gets weaker.
context.filter.env: How far the tone opens: four octaves as set.
context.fenv.attack: The length of the bloom, about 100 ms. This is what separates a trumpet from a synth stab.
context.fenv.sustain: How bright the note stays once the bloom has settled.
context.filter.kbd: High, so the line gets brighter as it climbs, the way a trumpet does.
context.aenv.sustain: At 10, so held notes keep their level.
context.glide.rate: About 45 ms on the overlapping notes: a join, not a swoop.
context.mod.lfoAmt: The widest vibrato the wheel can reach, about half a semitone each way.
context.mod.lfoRoute: WHEEL, so the vibrato only arrives as you push the wheel.
context.mod.toAFreq: Connects the WHEEL bus to Oscillator A’s pitch. OSC B FREQ is set the same way so both oscillators move together.

tweaks.hear: At 0 it is a hard synth stab. At 4.8 it blooms like a trumpet. At 6 the note has gone soft and horn-like.
The top of the line goes dull while the bottom stays bright: the tone is no longer even across the range.

tweaks.try: Raise to 3 and push the wheel fully
tweaks.hear: The vibrato widens to over two semitones each way and starts to sound like a siren rather than a player.
The bloom sharpens into a "wow" and the voice turns more electronic.

sounds.name: Hollow Clarinet
sounds.ref: In the style of a clarinet in its upper register
sounds.blurb: Soft, hollow single-oscillator voice with almost no movement in the tone.
sounds.how: A clarinet is one tube closed at the reed end, and a tube like that produces mainly odd harmonics. A square wave does exactly the same thing, so this is one oscillator, pulse on at width 5, and nothing else in the mixer. The filter sits at about 900 Hz to take the fizz off the top, and ENVELOPE AMOUNT is almost at 0: a clarinet does not change tone much during a note, so nothing should sweep. What is left to get right is the note shape, and that is all in the 34 ms attack and the short release.

steps.title: One square wave
steps.why:
A clarinet produces mainly odd harmonics, and so does a square wave. One square is the whole tone.
- Osc A pulse only, PULSE WIDTH 5 (50 %): at 5 the pulse is a true square, odd harmonics only, which is the hollow clarinet sound. Move it and that character goes.
- Osc A OCTAVE 2, FREQUENCY 0, SYNC off: a plain, in-tune oscillator.
- Osc B all waveforms off: B stays out of the sound. LO FREQ NORMAL and KYBD on leave it in its normal state.
- Listen for: a hollow, woody tone that is still bright and buzzy at the top, because the filter is open.

steps.title: Nothing else in the mixer
steps.why:
Nothing else goes into the mixer. A clarinet is one tube; a detuned partner would make it sound like two players.
- OSC A 7: the only source.
- OSC B 0, NOISE/EXT 0: no second oscillator and no noise.
- Listen for: the same hollow tone, a little quieter than before.

steps.title: Take the fizz off
steps.why:
The filter takes the fizz off the top of the square.
- CUTOFF 5.5 (about 890 Hz): rounds off the top. Higher is reedier and more like an oboe.
- RESONANCE 1: barely any, so there is no peak to colour the tone.
- KEYBOARD AMOUNT 9: the cutoff follows the notes almost exactly, so the top of the line is the same hollow colour as the bottom.
- Listen for: a softer, woody tone. Play high and low: the colour stays even.

steps.title: Almost no filter movement
steps.why:
The filter envelope (ADSR: attack, decay, sustain, release) is set to almost nothing, because a clarinet holds one colour through a note.
- ENVELOPE AMOUNT 0.8: a very small lift, just enough to hear the reed catch.
- ATTACK 10 ms, DECAY 170 ms: a quick, small movement that settles to SUSTAIN 4, then closes over RELEASE 87 ms after you let go.
- Listen for: turn ENVELOPE AMOUNT up to 4 and back. Any real sweep turns the clarinet into a synth lead.

steps.title: The reed takes a moment
steps.why:
The loudness envelope holds the whole character of the start of the note: soft, but not slow.
- ATTACK 34 ms: soft enough to hear the reed start, short enough to play a line with.
- DECAY 170 ms, SUSTAIN 10: full sustain, so the note holds while the key is down.
- RELEASE 87 ms: about 90 ms, so the note stops soon after you let go.
- Listen for: notes that swell in quickly rather than click. Try ATTACK at 0 to hear the click come back.

steps.title: Slur, do not re-tongue
steps.why:
Glide slurs overlapping notes, like a clarinettist changing notes without re-tonguing.
- RATE 1.4 (59 ms): a slide of about 60 ms between overlapping notes.
- Glide mode AUTO: slides only when you press a new key while still holding the last.
- Retrigger off: slurred notes keep going rather than starting again.
- Listen for: in the riff the fourth and fifth notes overlap. They join without a new attack.

steps.title: A waver on the mod wheel
steps.why:
The LFO (low-frequency oscillator, a slow modulation wave) is put on the mod wheel and sent to the filter, so a long note wavers in colour without going out of tune.
- LFO triangle on, FREQUENCY 6.5 (3.8 Hz): a smooth, fairly slow waver.
- AMOUNT LFO 3.5: at full wheel, the cutoff moves about six-tenths of an octave. Under 4 it stays a colour change rather than a tremolo.
- LFO route WHEEL: nothing happens until you push the mod wheel.
- To FILTER WH: the cutoff listens to the WHEEL bus.
- Listen for: hold a long note and push the wheel. The tone moves gently, the pitch stays put.

context.oscA.pw: At 5 this is a square wave: odd harmonics only, which is the clarinet. Move it and the odd-harmonic tone goes.
context.mix.oscB: At 0 on purpose. One tube, one oscillator.
context.filter.cutoff: Rounds off the top of the square. Higher is reedier and more like an oboe.
context.filter.env: Almost at 0, because a clarinet holds one colour through a note.
context.filter.kbd: At 9 the cutoff tracks the keyboard, so the tone is even across the range.
context.aenv.attack: About 34 ms: soft enough to hear the reed start, short enough to play a line with.
context.aenv.sustain: At 10, so the note holds while the key is down.
context.glide.mode: AUTO, so only the overlapping notes slide.
context.mode.retrig: Off, so slurred notes keep going rather than starting again.
context.mod.lfoAmt: How far the wheel can move the cutoff: about six-tenths of an octave at the top of the swing. Under 4 it stays a colour change rather than a tremolo.

tweaks.hear: The hollow clarinet thins out into a nasal, oboe-like tone as the even harmonics come back in.
Each note now sweeps open. It is a usable synth lead, but it is no longer a clarinet.
At 0 it clicks like an organ. At 3.5 it speaks. At 5 it is too slow to play a fast line.
The low, woody register of the instrument. The square wave gets darker and thicker.

sounds.name: Bassoon Reed Line
sounds.ref: In the style of a bassoon in its tenor register
sounds.blurb: Dark, buzzy double-reed voice for slow lines in the octave below middle C.
sounds.how: A double reed makes a narrow, buzzy pulse rather than a smooth wave, so Oscillator A is a pulse at width 3 with a sawtooth from Oscillator B underneath for weight. The filter is low, at about 480 Hz, which is where the bassoon’s body sits, and a moderate resonance picks out that band. Every note has a soft front: a 40 ms volume attack and a filter that opens over about 50 ms, which is how long a big reed takes to get going. The mod wheel moves the pulse width, so a held note can be made to buzz harder part-way through.

steps.title: Narrow pulse over a saw
steps.why:
A double reed makes a narrow, buzzy pulse, so the main voice is a thin pulse wave with a saw underneath for weight.
- Osc A pulse only, PULSE WIDTH 3 (31 %): thin and buzzy, like a reed being squeezed. Towards 5 it goes hollow and the reed character is lost.
- Osc B sawtooth only: supplies the body the pulse lacks.
- OCTAVE 2 on both, Osc A FREQUENCY 0, SYNC off: the same register.
- Osc B FREQUENCY +0.1: B a touch sharp, so the two move against each other slightly.
- LO FREQ NORMAL, KYBD on: B is an ordinary oscillator.
- Listen for: B is still at 0 in the mixer, so for now you hear just the thin buzz.

steps.title: Reed in front, body behind
steps.why:
The mixer puts the reed in front and the body behind it.
- OSC A 8: the reed you hear.
- OSC B 4: fills out the bottom. At 0 the sound is a thin buzz with nothing behind it.
- NOISE/EXT 0: no noise.
- Listen for: turn OSC B off and on. Without it the sound is all buzz and no instrument.

steps.title: Low and resonant
steps.why:
The filter is set low and resonant, which is where the bassoon’s body sits.
- CUTOFF 4.6 (about 480 Hz): lets the fundamental and low harmonics through. Above about 6 it stops sounding like a bassoon and starts sounding like an oboe.
- RESONANCE 3: picks out the band the instrument’s body rings at.
- ENVELOPE AMOUNT 3: about two and a half octaves of opening from the filter envelope on each note.
- KEYBOARD AMOUNT 8: keeps the top of the line from going dull.
- Listen for: a dark, buzzy, slightly nasal tone.

steps.title: A soft front on every note
steps.why:
The filter envelope (ADSR: attack, decay, sustain, release) gives every note a soft front. A big reed does not speak instantly.
- ATTACK 51 ms: the opening is spread over about 50 ms. At 0 the buzz arrives with the note and the sound turns electronic.
- DECAY 270 ms, SUSTAIN 4.5: after the opening, the tone settles a little darker for the held part.
- RELEASE 87 ms: closes quickly after the key comes up.
- Listen for: the buzz arriving just after the note does.

steps.title: Blown volume shape
steps.why:
The loudness envelope gives a blown shape, with the softest front of the woodwind voices because this is the biggest reed.
- ATTACK 43 ms: about 40 ms. The note swells in rather than clicking.
- DECAY 170 ms, SUSTAIN 10: full sustain, so held notes stay put.
- RELEASE 87 ms: about 90 ms, a clean stop.
- Listen for: soft note starts that still keep time. Compare ATTACK at 0 to hear how much more mechanical it becomes.

steps.title: Slur the overlaps
steps.why:
Glide slurs the overlapping notes, a little longer than the brighter voices because the line is slower.
- RATE 1.6 (77 ms): about an 80 ms slide.
- Glide mode AUTO: slides only when a new key goes down while the last is still held.
- Retrigger off: slurred notes do not start again.
- Listen for: the overlapping notes in the riff join smoothly with no new front.

steps.title: Buzz on the mod wheel
steps.why:
The LFO (low-frequency oscillator, a slow modulation wave) is put on the mod wheel and sent to Oscillator A’s PW (pulse width), so the reed can buzz harder and softer.
- LFO triangle on, FREQUENCY 6.2 (3.2 Hz): a smooth, slow swing.
- AMOUNT LFO 5: at full wheel the width swings from about 20 to about 42 per cent. Past about 7 the pulse gets so narrow at one end that the note thins out.
- LFO route WHEEL: nothing happens until you push the mod wheel.
- To OSC A PW WH: A’s pulse width listens to the WHEEL bus, so the gesture is a change of colour, not of pitch.
- Listen for: hold a note and push the wheel. The buzz thickens and thins about three times a second.

context.oscA.pw: At 3 the pulse is narrow and buzzy. Towards 5 it goes hollow and the reed character is lost.
context.mix.oscB: The saw that gives the note a body. At 0 the sound is a thin buzz with nothing behind it.
context.filter.cutoff: Low, which is what makes this dark. Above about 6 it stops sounding like a bassoon and starts sounding like an oboe.
context.filter.res: Picks out the band the instrument’s body rings at.
context.fenv.attack: The soft front. At 0 the buzz arrives with the note and the sound turns electronic.
context.aenv.attack: About 40 ms. Slower than the brighter voices, because a big reed takes longer to speak.
context.aenv.sustain: At 10, so held notes stay put.
context.glide.rate: About 80 ms on the overlapping notes.
context.mod.lfoAmt: How far the wheel swings the pulse width: from about 20 to about 42 per cent as set. Past about 7 the pulse gets so narrow at one end of the swing that the note thins out.
context.mod.toAPw: Connects the WHEEL bus to Oscillator A’s pulse width, so the gesture is a change of colour, not of pitch.

tweaks.hear: From hollow, to the buzzy double reed, to a thin nasal whine.
The register lifts and the voice turns into a reedy oboe rather than a bassoon.

tweaks.try: Set to 7, hold a long note and push the wheel halfway
tweaks.hear: The buzz swings much harder, and at the narrow end of each swing the note thins right out.
The buzz now arrives with the note instead of just after it, and the soft front is gone.

sounds.name: Flute with a Chiff
sounds.ref: In the style of a flute solo line
sounds.artist: Triangle wave with a noise chiff
sounds.blurb: Near-pure triangle voice with a short hiss of air at the start of every note.
sounds.how: A flute is close to a pure tone, so this is Oscillator B’s triangle on its own — the softest shape on the panel — with no second oscillator to thicken it. The character comes from the chiff: noise is left running in the mixer while the filter sits low enough to hide it, and a short, sharp filter envelope lets it through for about 85 ms at the start of each note. After that the filter closes again and only the tone is left. Vibrato is on the mod wheel, because a flute player starts a note straight and brings the vibrato in afterwards.

steps.title: One triangle
steps.why:
A flute is close to a pure tone, so the voice is one triangle wave, the softest shape on the panel.
- Osc B triangle only: very few harmonics, as close to a pure tone as this panel gets. It is the whole tone.
- Osc B OCTAVE 2, KYBD on: an ordinary oscillator following the keys.
- Osc A sawtooth and pulse off, SYNC off: Oscillator A is silent.
- Listen for: nothing yet. Oscillator B is still at 0 in the mixer, and A has no waveform on. The next step brings B up.

steps.title: Triangle plus standing noise
steps.why:
The triangle goes into the mixer with standing noise alongside it. The noise will become the chiff.
- OSC B 9: the flute tone.
- OSC A 0: a second oscillator would thicken the tone and lose the purity.
- NOISE/EXT 6: white noise, the air. It runs all the time, and the filter envelope will decide how much of it you hear. Past about 8 it is there through the whole note.
- Listen for: with the filter open, a soft tone with a lot of hiss through every note.

steps.title: Filter low enough to hide the noise
steps.why:
The filter is set low enough to hide the noise, while the triangle passes almost untouched because it has so little above the fundamental.
- CUTOFF 5.6 (about 960 Hz): most of the noise is cut. Raise it and the hiss is there through the whole note.
- RESONANCE 1.5: a slight boost at the cutoff.
- KEYBOARD AMOUNT 9: lifts the cutoff with the line, so the top notes keep their chiff.
- Listen for: the hiss drops to a faint haze and the tone comes through clean.

steps.title: Let the noise through for 85 ms
steps.why:
The filter envelope (ADSR: attack, decay, sustain, release) opens the filter for about 85 ms at the start of each note. That burst of noise is the chiff.
- ENVELOPE AMOUNT 4: opens the filter about three octaves. This sets how loud the chiff is.
- ATTACK 10 ms: gets there quickly.
- DECAY 85 ms: shuts it again in about 85 ms, so the chiff is short.
- SUSTAIN 0.5: near 0, so the filter stays shut after that and the held note is clean.
- RELEASE 34 ms: closes fast when you let go.
- Listen for: a short hiss on the front of each note, then a clean tone.

steps.title: Blown volume shape
steps.why:
The loudness envelope gives a blown shape, the quickest front of these woodwind voices because a flute speaks more readily than a reed.
- ATTACK 10 ms: a quick, soft start.
- DECAY 170 ms, SUSTAIN 10: held notes do not fade.
- RELEASE 72 ms: about 70 ms, a clean stop.
- Listen for: notes that start promptly with the chiff on top.

steps.title: Slur the overlaps
steps.why:
Glide slurs overlapping notes, and those slurred notes get no new chiff. That is the difference between a tongued note and a slurred one.
- RATE 1.2 (43 ms): a slide of about 45 ms.
- Glide mode AUTO: slides only when a new key goes down while the last is still held.
- Retrigger off: slurred notes do not restart the envelopes, so no chiff.
- Listen for: detached notes in the riff each get a hiss; overlapping ones join without one.

steps.title: Vibrato on the mod wheel
steps.why:
The LFO (low-frequency oscillator, a slow modulation wave) adds vibrato on the mod wheel, because a flute player starts a note straight and brings vibrato in afterwards.
- LFO triangle on, FREQUENCY 7 (5.1 Hz): a smooth wave at about five cycles a second.
- AMOUNT LFO 1.5: the depth at full wheel, a gentle vibrato.
- LFO route WHEEL: nothing happens until you push the wheel.
- To OSC B FREQ WH: Oscillator B is the only thing you can hear, so it is the one that needs to move. OSC A FREQ would do nothing here.
- Listen for: start a long note with the wheel down and push it halfway through.

context.oscB.tri: The whole tone. The triangle is the nearest thing to a pure note on this panel.
context.mix.oscA: At 0. A second oscillator would thicken the tone and lose the purity.
context.mix.noise: The air. It runs all the time, and the filter envelope decides how much of it you hear. Past about 8 it is there through the whole note.
context.filter.cutoff: Low enough to hide the noise between chiffs. Raise it and the hiss is there through the whole note.
context.filter.env: How loud the chiff is.
context.fenv.decay: How long the chiff lasts: about 85 ms as set.
context.fenv.sustain: Near 0, so the filter shuts again and the held note is clean.
context.aenv.attack: About 10 ms. A flute speaks more readily than a reed, so this is the quickest front of the five.
context.aenv.sustain: At 10, so held notes do not fade.
context.mod.toBFreq: Connects the WHEEL bus to Oscillator B’s pitch. Oscillator A is silent here, so OSC A FREQ would do nothing.

tweaks.hear: At 0 there is no chiff at all and the notes just appear. At 9 the hiss is loud enough to hear right through the note.
The chiff stretches from a tick into a long hiss at the front of each note.

tweaks.try: Set to 2.5, hold the long note and push the wheel in its second half
tweaks.hear: A straight note that opens into a wide, singer-like vibrato, the way a player shapes one.
The low register of the instrument: much softer, and the chiff becomes the loudest part of the note.

sounds.name: Deep Pulse-Width Knock
sounds.ref: In the style of the deep struck knocks used as abstract low percussion
sounds.blurb: A low struck knock with a hard front and almost nothing left behind it.
sounds.how: Oscillator A’s pulse is left as a sliver about eight per cent wide, which on its own is a thin, quiet buzz. The Pro-1 can send the filter envelope to that pulse width, and at full amount a 20 ms envelope throws the sliver open to a square and shuts it again. So the note starts with a full, loud low body and has collapsed back to the buzz 20 ms later, and that step is the knock. The filter never moves: it sits low and still, and all the movement is in the shape of the wave.

steps.title: A pulse with almost no width
steps.why:
Oscillator A’s pulse is squeezed to a sliver, which on its own is a thin, quiet buzz. Oscillator A is the whole sound; B is not used.
- Osc A pulse only: saw off, so the pulse width alone decides the tone.
- PULSE WIDTH 0.5 (8 %): a pulse about eight per cent wide. At 5 it would be a full, loud square; this near the end it almost disappears. This is the width the note falls back to after the knock.
- OCTAVE 1, FREQUENCY 0, SYNC off: low. With the riff’s keys the sound lands between 49 and 78 Hz.
- Osc B all waveforms off, NORMAL, KYBD on: B makes no sound and is not used as a modulator.
- Listen for: a thin, nasal low buzz. Nudge PULSE WIDTH towards 5 to hear the body it is missing, then put it back.

steps.title: Oscillator A alone in the mixer
steps.why:
Only Oscillator A feeds the filter.
- OSC A 9: the one source, well up.
- OSC B 0, NOISE/EXT 0: nothing else.
- Listen for: a thin low buzz and nothing more. Held notes keep sounding for now, because the volume shape comes later.

steps.title: Park the filter and leave it there
steps.why:
The filter is parked low and left there, so anything you hear at the front of the note has to come from somewhere else.
- CUTOFF 4.2 (about 364 Hz): a fixed lid that sets the weight of the knock. Higher lets more of the buzz through; lower makes it a duller thud.
- RESONANCE 2: a slight boost at the cutoff.
- ENVELOPE AMOUNT 0: on purpose, so the filter envelope does not sweep the cutoff. Only the pulse width will shape the front.
- KEYBOARD AMOUNT 2: very little tracking, so all the knocks keep the same weight.
- Listen for: the buzz gets darker and softer, still with no front edge.

steps.title: Send the filter envelope to the pulse width
steps.why:
The filter envelope (ADSR: attack, decay, sustain, release) is sent to the PW (pulse width) of Oscillator A instead of the cutoff. Each note throws the sliver open to a square and shuts it again. This is the whole trick.
- AMOUNT FIL ENV 10: full amount, the size of the knock. At 0 the knock is gone.
- FIL ENV route DIRECT, To OSC A PW DIR: the envelope goes onto the always-on bus, and A’s pulse width listens to it.
- ATTACK 2 ms, DECAY 20 ms, SUSTAIN 0: open at once and shut about 20 ms later. Longer decay gives the knock a short tuned body.
- RELEASE 23 ms: short, to match.
- Listen for: for that instant the note roughly doubles in level and gains its whole low body. A knock appears on the front, then the buzz.

steps.title: Knock-shaped volume
steps.why:
The loudness envelope makes the sound a knock with almost nothing behind it.
- ATTACK 2 ms: instant start, so the knock lands on the beat.
- DECAY 120 ms, SUSTAIN 0: the body falls away by itself in about a tenth of a second, so short taps and long presses all come out the same length.
- RELEASE 110 ms: finishes the note if you let go early.
- Listen for: a hard, low struck knock. Sweep DECAY between 3 and 6 to hear it go from a click to a thud with a tail.

context.mod.envAmt: The size of the knock. At 0 it is gone and a thin, quiet buzz is all that is left.
context.mod.toAPw: Connects the DIRECT bus, carrying the filter envelope, to Oscillator A’s pulse width. This is the whole trick.
context.fenv.decay: The length of the knock, about 20 ms. Longer settings give it a short tuned body.
context.oscA.pw: The width the note falls back to. At 0.5 it is a sliver, so almost nothing is left after the knock.
context.filter.cutoff: The weight of the knock. It does not move during the note.
context.filter.env: At 0 on purpose, so the only thing shaping the front of the note is the pulse width.
context.oscA.octave: At 1. With the riff’s keys the sound lands between 49 and 78 Hz.
context.aenv.decay: The length of the knock.

tweaks.try: Move from 0 to 10 while the riff plays
tweaks.hear: From a thin, quiet buzz to a full low knock, at about twice the level. Nothing else about the patch changes.
The width stays open for about 70 ms, so the knock grows a short tuned body instead of stopping dead.
The width no longer shuts down to nothing, so a low tuned tone rings on underneath the knock.
The lid comes off, and the knock turns into a bright hollow tap with much less weight.

sounds.name: Struck Sync Block
sounds.ref: In the style of the hard hollow stabs used as mid-range percussion
sounds.blurb: A hard, hollow strike whose tone dives through a set of overtones and stops.
sounds.how: With SYNC on, Oscillator A is restarted by every cycle of Oscillator B, so B holds the pitch and A’s FREQUENCY picks which overtone of that pitch you hear. The filter envelope is sent to A’s frequency, so each hit starts about fifteen semitones up the overtone series and falls back in 40 ms. Nothing sweeps the filter, so the whole character of the strike is that dive through the overtones.

steps.title: Oscillator B holds the pitch
steps.why:
Oscillator B is set up to hold the pitch. It will be the master of the sync, so it sets the note you hear, but it stays out of the mixer.
- Osc B sawtooth only, OCTAVE 2, FREQUENCY 0: a plain saw at the normal register.
- LO FREQ NORMAL, KYBD on: B follows the keys, so the keys set the pitch of the strike.
- OSC B 0: B is only the sync master; bringing it back into the mixer softens the effect.
- OSC A 9, NOISE/EXT 0: Oscillator A is the sound.
- Listen for: Oscillator A’s default saw for now. Nothing about B is audible yet.

steps.title: Sync Oscillator A on top of it
steps.why:
Sync (hard sync) forces Oscillator A to restart every time Oscillator B completes a cycle. B then sets the pitch, and A’s tuning picks which overtone of that pitch comes through. On the Pro-1 it is A that gets reset.
- Osc A sawtooth only, OCTAVE 3: a bright saw an octave up.
- FREQUENCY 1.5 (+2.1 st): with sync on this is a tone control, sitting about fourteen semitones above the note. Small moves change the colour of the hit, not its pitch.
- Sync on: without it A would be a free saw an octave and a bit above the note.
- Listen for: a hard, nasal, slightly vocal tone at B’s pitch. Turn Osc A FREQUENCY slowly and hear the tone change while the pitch stays.

steps.title: Throw the sync up and let it fall
steps.why:
The filter envelope (ADSR: attack, decay, sustain, release) is sent to the synced oscillator’s pitch. Because A is synced the note does not move: the overtone being picked out moves instead, and that dive is the strike.
- AMOUNT FIL ENV 8: about fifteen semitones of sweep on Oscillator A. Larger amounts give a harder, tearing edge.
- FIL ENV route DIRECT, To OSC A FREQ DIR: the envelope goes on the always-on bus, and A’s pitch listens to it.
- ATTACK 2 ms, DECAY 42 ms, SUSTAIN 0: each hit starts high and falls back in about 40 ms. This speed is what separates a strike from a swoop.
- RELEASE 49 ms: to match.
- Listen for: a fast downward sweep of tone on every note. Sweep DECAY up to 6 to hear it turn into the familiar sync swoop.

steps.title: A fixed, slightly peaked filter
steps.why:
The filter only takes the fizz off the top. Nothing sweeps it in this sound.
- CUTOFF 5.5 (about 890 Hz): a fixed lid.
- RESONANCE 2.5: a slight peak at the cutoff.
- ENVELOPE AMOUNT 0: the filter envelope stays off the filter; it is busy on Oscillator A.
- KEYBOARD AMOUNT 5: higher notes open the lid halfway as they rise.
- Listen for: the strike loses its harsh top and sounds more hollow and block-like.

steps.title: Strike-shaped volume
steps.why:
The loudness envelope turns each note into a short strike.
- ATTACK 2 ms: instant.
- DECAY 100 ms, SUSTAIN 0: the sound falls away in about a tenth of a second even if the key is held.
- RELEASE 110 ms: a touch longer than the decay, so a quick tap still gets its full fall.
- VOLUME 9: a synced saw carries less low end than a free one, so the output goes up to match the rest of the library. Turn it back to 7 before you move on.
- Listen for: a hard, hollow strike that dives through the overtones and stops.

context.oscA.sync: On. Without it Oscillator A is a free saw an octave and a bit above the note, and the envelope below turns into an ordinary pitch drop.
context.oscA.freq: The overtone the strike settles on. Small moves change the colour of the hit, not its pitch.
context.mod.envAmt: How far up the overtone series each hit starts. Large amounts give a harder, tearing edge.
context.mod.toAFreq: Connects the DIRECT bus, carrying the filter envelope, to the synced oscillator.
context.fenv.decay: The speed of the dive, about 40 ms. This is what separates a strike from a swoop.
context.mix.oscB: At 0. Oscillator B is only the sync master, and bringing it back softens the effect.
context.filter.cutoff: A fixed lid. Nothing sweeps it in this sound.
context.aenv.decay: The length of the strike.
context.out.volume: At 9 because a synced saw is quieter than a plain one. Turn it back to 7 before you move on.

tweaks.hear: The strike collapses into a plain falling blip, because the envelope is now bending a free oscillator’s pitch instead of its sync tone.
The pitch stays put and the hit walks up the overtone series, from hollow and woody to thin and reedy.
A small sweep is a soft knock. A large one tears across the overtones and sounds like metal.
The dive takes 170 ms and the strike turns into a short falling whoop.

sounds.name: Feedback Scrape
sounds.ref: In the style of the rough scraped textures used as percussion in electronic studio music
sounds.blurb: A short torn scrape with a rough grain that never settles into a pitch.
sounds.how: Two sawtooths are tuned three and a half semitones apart and run hotter than the filter input takes cleanly, so they already grind against each other. A cable then takes the MIXER output straight back into the EXT input, which adds the mixer to its own input. That loop sits ahead of the filter and the amplifier, so nothing holds it back: it drives the filter input far past its limit and turns the clash between the two saws into a torn, grainy scrape.

steps.title: Two saws, deliberately out of tune
steps.why:
Two saws are tuned to an interval nobody plays, so they clash and beat instead of blending.
- Osc A and B sawtooth only: two bright, buzzy waves.
- OCTAVE 3 on both: high, where the clash is harsh.
- Osc B FREQUENCY 2.5 (+3.5 st): three and a half semitones above A. Far enough to clash and near enough to beat.
- Osc A FREQUENCY 0, SYNC off: both free and following the keys.
- Listen for: B is still at 0 in the mixer, so for now you hear one saw. The clash arrives in the next step.

steps.title: Overload the filter input
steps.why:
Both oscillators go into the mixer hotter than the filter input takes cleanly. This is where the grain starts.
- OSC A 9, OSC B 8: high levels. The two add together and the tops of the waves are flattened before anything else happens.
- NOISE/EXT 0: no noise yet. This knob gets a different job in the last step.
- Listen for: a sour, beating clash with some roughness in it. Turn both down to 4 and the roughness goes, leaving two clean clashing saws.

steps.title: Keep the filter open enough to hear the grain
steps.why:
The filter stays open enough to let the grain through, since it sits well above the notes.
- CUTOFF 6.2 (about 1.4 kHz): below about 5 the scrape is cut away and a dull stab is left.
- RESONANCE 6: a clear peak at the cutoff for the loop to work against. It does less than it looks, because most of the grain comes from the overload.
- ENVELOPE AMOUNT 0: no sweep.
- KEYBOARD AMOUNT 4: higher keys scrape a little higher up.
- Listen for: a nasal, peaky clash.

steps.title: Short, hard volume shape
steps.why:
The loudness envelope makes each scrape one short burst.
- ATTACK 2 ms: instant.
- DECAY 50 ms, SUSTAIN 0: the sound is gone in about a twentieth of a second. This is the length of the scrape.
- RELEASE 60 ms: to match.
- Listen for: short, sharp bursts rather than held notes.

steps.title: Patch MIXER into EXT
steps.why:
A cable feeds the mixer back into itself, ahead of the filter and amplifier, so nothing holds the loop back.
