- MIXER to EXT: click MIXER, then EXT. MIXER sends the raw mix out; EXT is the external audio input. A cable in EXT switches the noise generator out.
- NOISE/EXT 8: now sets how much of the mixer goes back into itself, not a noise level. At 0 the scrape is gone.
- VOLUME 6: down to make up for the extra level. Put it back to 7 when you take the cable out.
- Listen for: the level jumps, the overload deepens, and the clash breaks up into a torn, grainy scrape. Sweep NOISE/EXT from 0 to 8 to hear it build.

context.mix.noise: With the cable in EXT this is how much of the mixer goes back into itself, not a noise level. At 0 the scrape is gone and two quiet clashing saws are left.
context.mix.oscA: High, to drive the filter input into overload before the loop even starts.
context.mix.oscB: Also high. The grain comes from the two levels added together.
context.oscB.freq: The interval between the saws. Three and a half semitones is far enough to clash and near enough to beat.
context.filter.res: A peak at the cutoff for the loop to work against. It does less here than it looks, because most of the grain comes from the overload.
context.filter.cutoff: How much of the grain gets through. Below about 5 the scrape is cut away and a dull stab is left.
context.filter.kbd: At 4, so higher keys scrape a little higher up.
context.aenv.decay: The length of the scrape.
context.out.volume: Down to 6 because the loop adds a lot of level. Put it back to 7 when you take the cable out.

tweaks.try: Move between 0 and 9 while the riff plays
tweaks.hear: At 0 it is a quiet, dry clashing stab. Towards 9 the loop takes over and the hit turns louder, rougher and unsteady.
At 5 the grain is cut away and a quiet dull stab is left. At 7.5 the scrape is bright and tearing.
In tune the two saws lock together and the hit drops to a plain low stab. Out of tune the scrape comes back.
The scrape lasts about 170 ms, which gives it time to settle into a ringing buzz.

sounds.name: Hollow Audio-Rate Rattle
sounds.ref: In the style of the dry rattles used as abstract upper-mid percussion
sounds.blurb: A dry, hollow rattle with a buzzing edge that does not belong to the note.
sounds.how: Oscillator B is taken off the keyboard, kept out of the mixer, and sent to Oscillator A’s pulse width through the modulation matrix. At about 310 Hz that is far too fast to hear as the usual pulse-width sweep: it chops the width hundreds of times a second and puts a dense set of extra tones around the note that do not line up with it. Short envelopes make it a hit, and because Oscillator B stays at one pitch every key gives a different rattle.

steps.title: A square wave up high
steps.why:
A square wave up high is the raw tone that will be chopped into a rattle.
- Osc A pulse only, PULSE WIDTH 5 (50 %): a square, hollow and plain.
- OCTAVE 3, FREQUENCY 0: high, around 1 kHz.
- Sync off: A runs free.
- Listen for: a plain hollow tone. The next steps set up what will chop it.

steps.title: Oscillator B fixed, and silent
steps.why:
Oscillator B is fixed at one pitch and kept silent. It is a modulator, not a sound.
- Osc B triangle only: the smoothest shape, which keeps the rattle from turning into a buzz-saw.
- OCTAVE 2, FREQUENCY 2 (+2.8 st): about 310 Hz. Treat FREQUENCY as a tone control: small moves rearrange which extra tones appear.
- Osc B keyboard off, LO FREQ NORMAL: B stays at about 310 Hz whatever you play, so every key gives a different rattle.
- OSC A 9, OSC B 0, NOISE/EXT 0: only A is heard.
- Listen for: no change yet. B is running but not heard or connected.

steps.title: Send Oscillator B to the pulse width
steps.why:
Oscillator B moves Oscillator A’s pulse width 310 times a second. PWM (pulse width modulation) is normally a slow sweep; at this speed it puts a dense set of extra tones around the note that do not line up with it.
- AMOUNT OSC B 8: the width is swung across more than half its range. At 0 the rattle is gone; at 10 it is almost noise.
- OSC B route DIRECT, To OSC A PW DIR: B goes on the always-on bus and A’s pulse width listens to it.
- Listen for: the clean square turns into a dry buzzing rattle. Play up the keyboard: each key sounds like a different object.

steps.title: A lid above the note, and a tick
steps.why:
The filter puts a lid above the note and a tick on the front.
- CUTOFF 8.2 (about 5.8 kHz): takes the fizz off the top without dulling the rattle. Lower settings give a duller knock.
- RESONANCE 4: a moderate peak at the cutoff.
- KEYBOARD AMOUNT 3: little tracking.
- ENVELOPE AMOUNT 2, DECAY 29 ms: the filter envelope (ADSR: attack, decay, sustain, release) opens the filter briefly, with a 2 ms attack, no sustain and a 34 ms release, for a harder tick on the front. Larger amounts turn every hit into a sweep and bury the rattle.
- Listen for: a slightly sharper front edge on each note.

steps.title: Rattle-shaped volume
steps.why:
The loudness envelope turns the rattle into a dry hit.
- ATTACK 2 ms: instant.
- DECAY 71 ms, SUSTAIN 0: about 70 ms and gone. This is the length of the rattle.
- RELEASE 87 ms: about the same, so the hits stay separate at the riff’s tempo.
- Listen for: short, dry, hollow rattles with a buzzing edge that does not belong to the note.

context.mod.oscBAmt: How far the width is swung. At 0 the rattle is gone and a plain hollow tap is left; at 10 it is almost noise.
context.mod.toAPw: Connects the DIRECT bus, carrying Oscillator B, to Oscillator A’s pulse width.
context.oscB.kbd: Off, so the modulator stays at one pitch and every key gives a different rattle.
context.oscB.freq: Tunes the modulator. Treat it as a tone control: small moves rearrange which extra tones appear.
context.oscB.tri: The triangle is the smoothest modulator shape and keeps the rattle from turning into a buzz-saw.
context.mix.oscB: At 0. Oscillator B is only heard through what it does to the pulse width.
context.filter.cutoff: How much of the extra buzz gets through. Lower settings give a duller knock.
context.filter.env: Small, for a tick on the front. Larger amounts turn every hit into a sweep and bury the rattle.
context.aenv.decay: The length of the rattle.

tweaks.hear: From a hollow tap, through a dry rattle, to a burst of buzzing noise.

tweaks.try: Sweep from −5 to 5 while tapping one key
tweaks.hear: The extra tones rearrange at every position. Most are sour, and a few line up and sound almost like a bell.
The modulator follows the keys, so every note rattles the same way and the sound becomes playable.
The width now starts near one edge, so the modulation pushes it right off and the rattle gains a stuttering, gated edge.

sounds.name: Bouncing Ratchet
sounds.ref: In the style of the short ratcheting bursts used as abstract percussion figures
sounds.blurb: A burst of hard bright ticks, like something small bouncing to a stop.
sounds.how: REPEAT re-fires both envelopes from the LFO for as long as a key is held, so one key press becomes a run of separate ticks at the LFO rate. Here the LFO is at about 15 Hz and both envelopes last around 25 ms, so each firing is a hard bright tick with silence after it. How long you hold the key decides how many ticks you get, and the riff holds different lengths so the bursts come out uneven.

steps.title: One narrow pulse, up high
steps.why:
One narrow pulse up high. A narrow pulse has plenty of high harmonics, which makes a tick read as hard rather than soft.
- Osc A pulse only, PULSE WIDTH 1.5 (17 %): thin and nasal. At 5 the ticks would be rounder and more hollow.
- OCTAVE 3, FREQUENCY 0, SYNC off: high, so the riff’s keys put the ticks between about 1 and 1.6 kHz.
- Osc B all waveforms off: B is not used.
- OSC A 9, OSC B 0, NOISE/EXT 0: only A in the mixer.
- Listen for: a thin, reedy held tone for now.

steps.title: A bright peak
steps.why:
The filter puts a bright peak where the ticks cut through.
- CUTOFF 7.6 (about 3.8 kHz): where the ticks sit. Lower makes them woody; higher makes them glassy.
- RESONANCE 6: narrows each tick to a band, so it reads as a small hard object rather than a click.
- KEYBOARD AMOUNT 4: some tracking.
- ENVELOPE AMOUNT 2.5, DECAY 20 ms: the filter envelope (ADSR: attack, decay, sustain, release) opens the filter for 20 ms to harden the front, with a 2 ms attack, no sustain and a 23 ms release.
- Listen for: a peaky, bright tone with a small click at the start.

steps.title: Very short ticks
steps.why:
The loudness envelope makes each note a very short tick.
- ATTACK 2 ms: instant.
- DECAY 24 ms, SUSTAIN 0: about 25 ms, then silence. Longer settings run the ticks together into a buzz later.
- RELEASE 28 ms: to match.
- Listen for: a held key now gives one short tick and then silence.

steps.title: Let the LFO fire the ticks
steps.why:
REPEAT lets the LFO (low-frequency oscillator, which also runs the clock here) re-fire both envelopes while a key is held.
- Repeat on: one key press becomes a run of separate ticks at the LFO rate. Without it there is one tick per key press.
- Drone off: the gate is not held open, so REPEAT can fire it.
- FREQUENCY · lfo rate 8.8 (15 Hz): the envelopes fire about every 68 ms. Lower gives a slower rattle you can count.
- Listen for: bursts of hard, bright ticks. The LFO free-runs, so the first tick does not land with the key and no two bursts match. Hold longer for more ticks.

context.mode.repeat: The LFO re-fires both envelopes while a key is held. Without it this is one tick per key press and there is no ratchet.
context.lfo.rate: The spacing of the ticks: 8.8 is about 15 Hz. Lower settings give a slower rattle you can count.
context.aenv.decay: The length of each tick. Longer settings run the ticks together into a buzz.
context.aenv.sustain: At 0, so there is silence between the ticks rather than a held tone under them.
context.oscA.pw: Narrow, for a hard thin tick. At 5 the ticks are rounder and more hollow.
context.filter.cutoff: Where the ticks sit. Lower settings make them woody, higher ones make them glassy.
context.filter.res: Narrows each tick to a band, so it reads as a small hard object rather than a click.
context.oscA.octave: At 3, so the riff’s keys put the ticks between about 1 and 1.6 kHz.

tweaks.hear: From a slow rattle you can count to a fast trill that almost turns into a pitch.
The ticks lengthen past the gap between them and the ratchet turns into a rough buzzing tone.
Woody and dull: more like a small wooden thing being knocked than a hard bright tick.
One tick per key press, so the riff becomes a sparse set of taps.

sounds.name: Resonance-Spike Air Ping
sounds.ref: In the style of the thin airy pings used as top-end percussion
sounds.blurb: A very high, thin ping over a short puff of air, right at the top of hearing.
sounds.how: Noise goes into a filter set near 14 kHz, with the resonance well short of the point where the filter whistles on its own. On the panel that is a plain puff of air and nothing else. A cable then takes FILTER ENV into RESO CV, so each hit pushes the resonance past that point and drops it back 50 ms later, and you hear a thin ping on top of the puff. KEYBOARD AMOUNT stays at 0, because any tracking would push the cutoff out of hearing on the upper keys.

steps.title: Noise only
steps.why:
Only noise goes into the filter. There are no oscillators anywhere in this sound.
- OSC A 0, OSC B 0: both oscillators out.
- NOISE/EXT 6: white noise, a hiss with energy at all frequencies. It is the puff of air the ping will sit on, and the only thing feeding the filter.
- Listen for: a steady hiss while a key is held.

steps.title: The filter right at the top
steps.why:
The filter is set right at the top of hearing, with the resonance short of the point where the filter whistles by itself.
- CUTOFF 9.5 (about 14 kHz): only the very top of the noise gets through. Below about 8 it stops sounding like air.
- RESONANCE 6: a strong peak at the cutoff, but not enough to whistle. At 10 it would whistle all the time.
- ENVELOPE AMOUNT 0: the filter envelope does not move the cutoff.
- KEYBOARD AMOUNT 0: on purpose. Any tracking would push the cutoff above hearing on the upper keys and the sound would go.
- Listen for: a thin, airy hiss with no pitch in it.

steps.title: A short spike shape
steps.why:
The filter envelope (ADSR: attack, decay, sustain, release) is shaped into a short spike, though for now it is driving nothing.
- ATTACK 2 ms: instant rise.
- DECAY 50 ms, SUSTAIN 0: falls to nothing in about 50 ms. This will be the length of the ping.
- RELEASE 60 ms: to match.
- Listen for: no change. With ENVELOPE AMOUNT at 0 the envelope has no job until the cable goes in.

steps.title: Patch FILTER ENV into RESO CV
steps.why:
A cable sends the filter envelope to the resonance, so each hit pushes the filter briefly past the point where it whistles.
- FILTER ENV to RESO CV: click FILTER ENV, then RESO CV. FILTER ENV sends the envelope out as a voltage; RESO CV (control voltage) adds to the RESONANCE knob. A full envelope adds a full turn of resonance.
- Listen for: a thin ping appearing at the top of the puff on every note, gone again 50 ms later. Pull the cable and it goes.

steps.title: Hit-shaped volume
steps.why:
The loudness envelope makes the whole thing a short hit.
- ATTACK 2 ms: instant.
- DECAY 35 ms, SUSTAIN 0: about 35 ms and gone. This is the length of the whole hit.
- RELEASE 34 ms: to match.
- VOLUME 10: a band of noise this high up has very little energy, so the output goes up. Turn it back to 7 before you move on.
- Listen for: a very high, thin ping over a short puff of air.

context.filter.res: The resting resonance. It is short of the point where the filter whistles, so the panel on its own gives no ping; the cable is what carries it past. At 10 it whistles all the time and the hits stop standing out.
context.filter.cutoff: The pitch of the ping, about 14 kHz. Below about 8 it stops sounding like air.
context.filter.kbd: At 0 on purpose. Any tracking pushes the cutoff out of hearing on the upper keys.
context.filter.env: At 0. The filter envelope does nothing to the cutoff here; it only feeds the cable.
context.fenv.decay: The length of the ping, about 50 ms.
context.mix.noise: The puff of air the ping sits on, and the only thing feeding the filter.
context.aenv.decay: The length of the whole hit.
context.out.volume: At 10 because there is very little energy this far up. Turn it back to 7 before you move on.

tweaks.hear: The spike lasts about 170 ms and the ping becomes a short high whistle.
The ping drops to about 7 kHz and the hit sounds more like a small metal object than air.
At 3 the ping is almost bare. At 10 there is a broad puff of air around it.

tweaks.try: Raise to 5 and play an octave up
tweaks.hear: The cutoff tracks the keys, the ping thins out and then disappears above hearing. This is why it is left at 0.

sounds.name: Poly-Mod Glass Bells
sounds.ref: In the style of Prophet-5 Poly-Mod bell sounds
sounds.blurb: Clear, ringing bells with a slightly clashing set of overtones and a low hum under each note.
sounds.how: A bell does not have overtones in a neat row like a string: some fall between the notes of the scale. Here Oscillator B is kept out of the mixer and sent to Oscillator A’s pitch through the modulation matrix, tuned a tritone above it. It moves A’s pitch hundreds of times a second, which adds new tones above and below the note that are not in the harmonic series. That is frequency modulation, done with an analogue oscillator, and it is the Prophet-5’s Poly-Mod trick that most monosynths cannot do. B follows the keyboard, so every key gives the same bell.

steps.title: A square wave to be modulated
steps.why:
A square wave is the tone that will be modulated into a bell. It is the only thing in the mixer.
- Osc A pulse only, PULSE WIDTH 5 (50 %): a square, hollow and plain.
- OCTAVE 2, SYNC off: the normal register, free-running.
- OSC A 8, OSC B 0, NOISE/EXT 0: just A.
- Listen for: a plain, hollow held tone.

steps.title: Oscillator B a tritone up, out of the mixer
steps.why:
Oscillator B is tuned a tritone above A and kept out of the mixer. You will not hear it, only what it does to Oscillator A.
- Osc B triangle only: the smoothest shape, so the modulation is clean.
- OCTAVE 2, FREQUENCY 4.3 (+6 st): six semitones up, a tritone. This interval decides which overtones appear; a tritone gives a bell, other settings give other metals.
- Osc B keyboard on, LO FREQ NORMAL: B moves with the keys, so the interval is the same on every key and every note is the same bell.
- Listen for: no change yet. B is at 0 in the mixer.

steps.title: Send B to A’s pitch
steps.why:
Oscillator B moves Oscillator A’s pitch hundreds of times a second. That is FM (frequency modulation), done with analogue parts; Sequential called it Poly-Mod on the Prophet-5. It adds tones above and below the note that fall between the notes of the scale, as a bell’s overtones do.
- AMOUNT OSC B 6: how clangy the bell is. Lower is purer and more like glass; higher adds more clashing tones.
- OSC B route DIRECT, To OSC A FREQ DIR: B on the always-on bus, and A’s pitch listens to it.
- Osc A FREQUENCY −0.5: the modulation pulls A about two-thirds of a semitone sharp, so this brings it back in tune. If you change AMOUNT OSC B, retune here.
- Listen for: the plain square turns into a clangy, bell-like tone.

steps.title: A long, struck fade
steps.why:
The filter and both envelopes turn the held tone into a struck bell that rings out.
- CUTOFF 5.5 (about 890 Hz): with RESONANCE 0 and KEYBOARD AMOUNT 8. Lower for a soft, distant bell; higher for a hard, bright one.
- ENVELOPE AMOUNT 3.5, DECAY 1.0 s: with SUSTAIN 0, the filter envelope (ADSR: attack, decay, sustain, release) makes the first moment of each strike a little brighter, then settles.
- Loudness DECAY 5.1 s, RELEASE 6.1 s: with a 2 ms attack and no sustain, an instant strike and a five-second fade. Each bell rings out on its own, even after you let go.
- Retrigger on: every key press gives a fresh strike.
- Listen for: bright strikes that mellow and ring for several seconds.

context.mod.oscBAmt: In this sound: how clangy the bell is. Lower is purer and more like a glass; higher adds more clashing tones and pulls the pitch further sharp.
context.oscB.freq: In this sound: the interval between the two oscillators, which decides which overtones appear. A tritone gives a bell; other settings give other metals.
context.oscB.kbd: In this sound: on, so the interval stays the same on every key and every note is the same bell.
context.mix.oscB: In this sound: at 0. Oscillator B is only a modulator here.
context.oscA.freq: In this sound: corrects the sharpening that the modulation causes. If you change AMOUNT OSC B, retune here.
context.aenv.decay: In this sound: how long each bell rings.
context.filter.cutoff: In this sound: lower for a soft, distant bell; higher for a hard, bright one.

tweaks.hear: From a nearly pure tone to a heavy, clashing bell. Retune with Oscillator A’s FREQUENCY as you go.
A different set of overtones: a brighter, more gong-like bell.
B stays at one pitch, so every key gives a different metal. Good for effects, not for tunes.

sounds.name: Poly-Mod Electric Piano
sounds.ref: In the style of an FM electric piano of the 1980s
sounds.blurb: A warm electric piano with a soft bark at the start of each note and a gentle, slow shimmer as it fades.
sounds.how: The bark of an electric piano comes from overtones that are strong for a moment and then die away. Oscillator B is tuned to the same note as Oscillator A and sent to A’s pitch through the modulation matrix, which is frequency modulation at a one-to-one ratio: it thickens A’s square wave with extra harmonics. The filter envelope lets those harmonics through at the start of each note and then closes, so the bark fades and a round tone is left. Oscillator B is also turned up a little in the mixer, so it is a modulator and a voice at the same time.

steps.title: A square wave and a triangle at the same pitch
steps.why:
A square and a triangle at the same pitch are the raw material for the piano. Oscillator B will soon be a modulator as well as a quiet voice.
- Osc A pulse only, PULSE WIDTH 5 (50 %): a square, hollow and fairly soft.
- Osc A OCTAVE 2, SYNC off: the normal register, free-running.
- Osc B triangle only, OCTAVE 2, FREQUENCY 0: the same note as A, a round, pure tone.
- KYBD on, LO FREQ NORMAL: B follows the keys, so it stays on A’s pitch everywhere.
- OSC A 7, OSC B 2.5, NOISE/EXT 0: the square leads and the triangle sits softly under it.
- Listen for: a plain, hollow organ-like tone with a slightly rounder bottom.

steps.title: B modulates A
steps.why:
Oscillator B moves Oscillator A’s pitch at audio rate. That is FM (frequency modulation), which Sequential called Poly-Mod on the Prophet-5. At a one-to-one ratio it adds extra harmonics to A’s square.
- AMOUNT OSC B 6: how hard the bark is. At 0 you are left with a plain square and triangle.
- OSC B route DIRECT, To OSC A FREQ DIR: B goes onto the always-on bus and A’s pitch listens to it.
- Osc A FREQUENCY −0.5: the modulation pulls A sharp, so this puts it back on the note. The small mismatch that is left makes the tone shimmer slowly as it fades.
- Listen for: the square takes on a harder, reedier tone. Turn AMOUNT OSC B down and up to hear it.

steps.title: Let the bark through, then close
steps.why:
The filter lets the bark through at the start of each note and then closes, so a round tone is left.
- CUTOFF 5 (about 630 Hz), RESONANCE 0: the resting tone is round, with the extra harmonics trimmed.
- KEYBOARD AMOUNT 8: higher notes stay nearly as bright as low ones.
- ENVELOPE AMOUNT 4: how much of the bark gets through at the start. More is harder and more metallic.
- Filter DECAY 600 ms, SUSTAIN 0: with a 2 ms attack and 570 ms release, the filter envelope (ADSR: attack, decay, sustain, release) opens at once and closes over about 0.6 s. That is how long the bark lasts.
- Listen for: each note starts with the full reedy tone and settles to a round one.

steps.title: A piano’s fade
steps.why:
The loudness envelope gives the note a piano’s fade: struck, then dying away even while held.
- ATTACK 2 ms: instant.
- DECAY 5.1 s, SUSTAIN 0: a five-second fall to silence, so a held note dies away like a struck key.
- RELEASE 570 ms: a short tail if you let go early.
- Retrigger on: RETRIG restarts both envelopes on every key press, so every note gets its own bark.
- Listen for: a bark on each note and a slow, gentle shimmer as it fades. Play chords one note at a time and let them ring.

context.mod.oscBAmt: In this sound: how hard the bark is. At 0 you are left with a plain square and triangle.
context.mix.oscB: In this sound: Oscillator B heard as a soft triangle under the square. It keeps modulating whatever this is set to.
context.oscA.freq: In this sound: corrects the sharpening the modulation causes. The small mismatch that is left makes the tone shimmer slowly as it fades.
context.filter.env: In this sound: how much of the bark gets through at the start of each note.
context.fenv.decay: In this sound: how long the bark lasts before the tone turns round.
context.aenv.decay: In this sound: how long each note rings.

tweaks.hear: From a soft, mellow piano to a hard, glassy one. Retune with Oscillator A’s FREQUENCY at 7.
The modulator an octave up gives a hollow, more bell-like piano.
A brighter, more percussive attack, like a piano played harder.

sounds.name: Bowed Glass Pad
sounds.ref: In the style of a glass harmonica or a bowed wine glass
sounds.blurb: A slow, glassy tone that swells in, with faint clashing overtones that bloom and settle.
sounds.how: A rubbed glass or a bowed metal bar gives a pure note with a few thin overtones that do not fit the harmonic series. Oscillator B, out of the mixer and tuned about two and three-quarter times higher than Oscillator A, modulates A’s pitch through the modulation matrix. That frequency modulation puts those out-of-series tones round the note. Slow attacks on both envelopes make it swell like a bowed sound, not a struck one, and the filter opens over about a second so the overtones arrive after the note.

steps.title: A square wave on its own
steps.why:
A square wave on its own is the tone that will be turned to glass.
- Osc A pulse only, PULSE WIDTH 5 (50 %): a hollow square.
- OCTAVE 2, SYNC off: normal register, free.
- OSC A 6, OSC B 0, NOISE/EXT 0: only A in the mixer. B will be a modulator only.
- Listen for: a plain, hollow held tone.

steps.title: Oscillator B well above, between the harmonics
steps.why:
Oscillator B goes well above A, at a pitch that falls between A’s harmonics.
- Osc B triangle only: the smoothest shape for a modulator.
- OCTAVE 3, FREQUENCY 4 (+5.6 st): together these put B about 2.76 times A’s pitch. That ratio is not a whole number, which is what makes the overtones glassy rather than musical. Small moves change which glassy tones appear.
- KYBD on, LO FREQ NORMAL: B follows the keys, so the ratio stays the same on every note.
- Listen for: no change yet. B is at 0 in the mixer and not connected.

steps.title: B modulates A
steps.why:
Oscillator B moves A’s pitch at audio rate. That is FM (frequency modulation) done with analogue parts, and it puts thin tones round the note that are not in the harmonic series, as a rubbed glass has.
- AMOUNT OSC B 6: how many of the thin overtones are heard. Lower is a purer glass.
- OSC B route DIRECT, To OSC A FREQ DIR: B on the always-on bus, and A’s pitch listens to it.
- Osc A FREQUENCY −0.5: about −0.46, which brings the note back in tune after the modulation pulls it sharp.
- Listen for: the square gains a cold, metallic, slightly clashing ring.

steps.title: Swell in, bloom, settle
steps.why:
Slow envelopes make it swell like a bowed sound, not a struck one. ADSR is attack, decay, sustain, release.
- Loudness ATTACK 860 ms, SUSTAIN 10: the volume fades in over nearly a second. At 0 it becomes a struck bell.
- Loudness RELEASE 6.1 s: each note hangs for about six seconds after you let go.
- CUTOFF 5.5 (about 890 Hz): with RESONANCE 0 and KEYBOARD AMOUNT 8, a soft resting tone that stays even across the keys.
- ENVELOPE AMOUNT 2, filter ATTACK 1.3 s: with DECAY 2.5 s and SUSTAIN 5, the filter takes about 1.3 s to open, then falls back halfway. The overtones bloom after the note arrives.
- Listen for: each note swells in, brightens, then settles. Let go and it rings for a long time.

context.oscB.freq: In this sound: with OCTAVE 3, sets the ratio between the two oscillators. Small moves change which glassy tones appear.
context.mod.oscBAmt: In this sound: how many of the thin overtones are heard. Lower is a purer glass.
context.oscA.freq: In this sound: brings the note back in tune after the modulation has pulled it sharp.
context.fenv.attack: In this sound: how long the overtones take to bloom after the note starts.
context.aenv.attack: In this sound: the swell. At 0 it becomes a struck bell.
context.aenv.release: In this sound: how long each note hangs after you let go.

tweaks.hear: The swell goes and the note is struck, like a bell or a vibraphone.
Only a faint shimmer is left above a nearly pure tone.

tweaks.try: Move slowly between 3 and 5 while holding a note
tweaks.hear: The glassy tones slide and cross each other as the ratio changes.

sounds.name: Strings with Key-Tracked Shimmer
sounds.ref: In the style of 1970s string-machine ensembles
sounds.blurb: Soft, slowly moving strings whose shimmer is slow on low notes and quicker on high ones.
sounds.how: Normally the LFO moves pulse width, and it moves at the same speed on every note. Here Oscillator B does the job instead. B is sent to Oscillator A’s pulse width through the modulation matrix, tuned eight cents away from A. Because B runs at nearly the same pitch as A, the width moves at the difference between the two: about once a second on A3 and twice a second an octave up, just as the beating in a real string section speeds up with pitch. B is also quiet in the mixer, adding a detuned voice. Slow attacks on both envelopes make it strings.

steps.title: Saw and pulse on Oscillator A
steps.why:
Oscillator A gets both of its shapes at once. The saw gives the string buzz; the pulse is what will move.
- Osc A sawtooth and pulse on: the Pro-1’s waveform switches add together. The saw is unaffected by pulse width, so it keeps the tone full.
- PULSE WIDTH 5 (50 %): the pulse starts as a square.
- OCTAVE 2, FREQUENCY 0, SYNC off: plain and in tune.
- OSC A 7, NOISE/EXT 0: A in the mixer, no noise.
- Listen for: a bright, static, organ-like tone.

steps.title: Oscillator B eight cents sharp
steps.why:
Oscillator B is tuned about eight cents sharp. It will drive the shimmer, and it also adds a quiet second voice.
- Osc B triangle only: smooth, both as a voice and as a modulator.
- OCTAVE 2, FREQUENCY +0.1: B about eight cents (0.06 on the knob) above A. The detune sets the speed of the shimmer; further from 0 is faster on every note.
- KYBD on, LO FREQ NORMAL: B follows the keys at audio rate.
- OSC B 2.5: just enough to add a detuned voice. At 0 you hear the width movement alone.
- Listen for: a slow, gentle beating in the tone.

steps.title: B moves A’s pulse width
steps.why:
Oscillator B moves Oscillator A’s pulse width. PWM (pulse width modulation) normally uses the LFO at one fixed speed. Here the width moves at the difference between A and B, so it speeds up with pitch, as the beating in a real string section does.
- AMOUNT OSC B 6.5: how far the pulse width swings. Too much and the notes start to pulse in level.
- OSC B route DIRECT, To OSC A PW DIR: A’s pulse width listens to the always-on bus carrying B.
- Listen for: hold a low note, then a high one. On A3 the shimmer is about once a second; an octave up it is about twice a second.

steps.title: Bowed envelopes
steps.why:
Bowed envelopes, with ADSR (attack, decay, sustain, release) shapes on both filter and volume, turn the tone into strings.
- Loudness ATTACK 380 ms, RELEASE 1.5 s: with SUSTAIN 10, a slow start that makes it strings rather than an organ, and a long tail so notes overlap as you move along a line.
- CUTOFF 5.5 (about 890 Hz): with RESONANCE 1 and KEYBOARD AMOUNT 6, a mellow resting tone that stays fairly even across the keys.
- ENVELOPE AMOUNT 1.5, filter ATTACK 380 ms: with DECAY 1.0 s and SUSTAIN 7, the filter opens a little as each note starts, like a bow biting.
- Listen for: soft entries, a slight brightening, and chords that blur into each other as you change.

context.oscB.freq: In this sound: the detune, and so the speed of the shimmer. Further from 0 is faster on every note.
context.mod.oscBAmt: In this sound: how far the pulse width swings. Too much and the notes start to pulse in level.
context.mod.toAPw: In this sound: listens to the DIRECT bus, which carries Oscillator B.
context.mix.oscB: In this sound: the detuned second voice. At 0 you hear the width movement alone.
context.aenv.attack: In this sound: the slow start that makes it strings rather than an organ.
context.aenv.release: In this sound: lets each note overlap the next as you move along a line.

tweaks.hear: The shimmer becomes a fast, nervous flutter on high notes.
Only the moving pulse width is left: thinner, but you can hear the shimmer clearly.

tweaks.try: Flip to WHEEL and OSC A PW to WH
tweaks.hear: The strings are still until you push the mod wheel.

sounds.name: Singing Lead with Waking Vibrato
sounds.ref: In the style of a singer who starts a long note straight and lets the vibrato grow
sounds.blurb: A warm, singing lead whose vibrato starts slow on each note and speeds up as the note is held.
sounds.how: The LFO gives a gentle vibrato to both oscillators. A cable from FILTER ENV into LFO CV then makes the filter envelope set the LFO’s speed. The envelope rises over about three seconds, so a new note starts with the pitch drifting slowly and the vibrato speeds up to about five times a second as you hold it. When you let go the envelope falls and the vibrato slows again as the note dies away. The same envelope also opens the filter a little, so held notes brighten as the vibrato wakes up.

steps.title: A saw with a triangle above
steps.why:
A saw with a triangle an octave above, exactly in tune so they blend without beating.
- Osc A sawtooth only, OCTAVE 2, FREQUENCY 0: the main voice, full and buzzy.
- Osc B triangle only, OCTAVE 3, FREQUENCY 0: an octave up, soft, adding a sweeter top.
- SYNC off, KYBD on, LO FREQ NORMAL: both free and following the keys.
- OSC A 7, OSC B 4, NOISE/EXT 0: the saw leads.
- Listen for: a bright, warm tone with a clear upper octave. Mute OSC B to hear what it adds.

steps.title: A soft vibrato on both oscillators
steps.why:
The LFO (low-frequency oscillator, a slow wave for moving other controls) gives a soft vibrato to both oscillators. For now it runs slowly.
- LFO triangle on, FREQUENCY 3.7 (0.7 Hz): a smooth wave at a slow speed. This is the speed the vibrato starts at.
- AMOUNT LFO 1: about a quarter of a semitone either way. The depth stays the same at every speed.
- LFO route DIRECT: always on.
- To OSC A FREQ DIR, To OSC B FREQ DIR: both pitches listen, so the two oscillators stay together.
- Listen for: a slow, lazy drift in pitch, less than once a second.

steps.title: Patch FILTER ENV into LFO CV
steps.why:
A cable lets the filter envelope set the LFO’s speed, so the vibrato wakes up as the note is held.
- FILTER ENV to LFO CV: click FILTER ENV, then LFO CV (control voltage for the LFO speed). The envelope adds up to three octaves of speed on top of the knob.
- Filter ATTACK 2.9 s, SUSTAIN 10: the envelope (ADSR: attack, decay, sustain, release) rises over about three seconds and stays at the top. That is how long the vibrato takes to reach full speed, about 5.6 Hz, eight times the start.
- DECAY 1.0 s, RELEASE 570 ms: when you let go, the envelope falls and the vibrato slows as the note dies.
- Listen for: hold a long note. The pitch drifts slowly at first, then the vibrato speeds up to a singer’s pace.

steps.title: A rounded voice
steps.why:
The filter, volume shape and glide finish the voice.
- CUTOFF 4.8 (about 550 Hz), RESONANCE 2: with KEYBOARD AMOUNT 7, a rounded, slightly vocal tone that does not go dull higher up.
- ENVELOPE AMOUNT 1.5: kept small, so held notes open only slightly. The envelope’s main job is the vibrato speed.
- Loudness ATTACK 76 ms, RELEASE 570 ms: with SUSTAIN 10, a soft start and a short tail.
- RATE 2.5 (190 ms), Glide mode AUTO: slides only between overlapping notes. Legato notes also keep the envelope going, so the vibrato stays at speed through a slur.
- Listen for: long notes that brighten a little as the vibrato wakes up. Play legato to hear the vibrato carry on through the slide.

context.fenv.attack: In this sound: how long the vibrato takes to reach full speed.
context.lfo.rate: In this sound: the speed the vibrato starts at. The cable adds up to three octaves of speed on top.
context.mod.lfoAmt: In this sound: the depth of the vibrato, the same at every speed.
context.mod.toBFreq: In this sound: gives Oscillator B the same vibrato, so the two oscillators stay together.
context.filter.env: In this sound: kept small. The envelope’s main job is to drive the LFO speed through the cable.
context.glide.mode: In this sound: AUTO slides only between overlapping notes. Legato notes also keep the envelope going, so the vibrato stays at speed through a slur.

tweaks.hear: The vibrato reaches full speed in under a second.
A wider, more operatic vibrato.
The note starts almost still and the vibrato ends up slower, about 2.8 Hz.

sounds.name: Slow Vowel Pad
sounds.ref: In the style of wordless synth choirs in 1980s film scores
sounds.blurb: A soft, sustained pad whose tone moves slowly between "ooh" and "aah".
sounds.how: With SYNC on, Oscillator A restarts every time Oscillator B completes a cycle, so B sets the pitch and A’s frequency only changes the tone. On the Pro-1 it is A that follows B, the reverse of most synths, which means the LFO sent to OSC A FREQ changes the tone without moving the pitch. A very slow LFO, one cycle in about seven seconds, moves A through a range of about an octave. That moves a peak through the harmonics of the note, and the ear hears it as a vowel changing. Oscillator B is also in the mixer, so the note keeps a steady body under the moving part.

steps.title: Sync A to B
steps.why:
Sync (hard sync) makes Oscillator A restart every time Oscillator B completes a cycle. B sets the pitch and A’s tuning only changes the tone. On the Pro-1 it is A that follows B, the reverse of most synths.
- Osc A sawtooth, OCTAVE 3, Sync on: A is the moving vowel part, FREQUENCY at 0. OCTAVE 3 puts the vowel round the second harmonic of the note.
- Osc B triangle only, OCTAVE 2, FREQUENCY 0: B sets the pitch you hear. KYBD on, LO FREQ NORMAL.
- OSC A 7, OSC B 4, NOISE/EXT 0: B in the mixer gives a steady body under the moving part.
- Listen for: a bright, slightly nasal tone at B’s pitch.

steps.title: A very slow LFO on A’s frequency
steps.why:
A very slow LFO (low-frequency oscillator) moves A’s frequency. With sync on that changes the tone, not the pitch, and the ear hears it as a vowel changing.
- LFO triangle on, FREQUENCY 1.1 (0.15 Hz): one cycle in about seven seconds. Above about 5 it starts to sound like a talking effect.
- AMOUNT LFO 5: swings A six semitones either way. This is how wide the vowel moves.
- LFO route DIRECT, To OSC A FREQ DIR: always on, A’s pitch listening.
- Listen for: hold a note. The tone drifts from “ooh” to “aah” and back. Switch SYNC off to hear the pitch of A bend instead.

steps.title: A soft filter
steps.why:
The filter takes the edge off the sync so it sounds like a voice.
- CUTOFF 5.8 (about 1.1 kHz): trims the harsh top of the synced saw.
- RESONANCE 3: a slight peak that makes the tone more vocal.
- KEYBOARD AMOUNT 7: the cutoff follows the keys most of the way.
- ENVELOPE AMOUNT 0: no sweep, so the only movement is the vowel.
- Listen for: a softer, choir-like tone with the vowel still moving underneath.

steps.title: Fade in and out
steps.why:
The loudness envelope fades each note in and out, like a choir.
- ATTACK 570 ms: about half a second to fade in.
- DECAY 1.0 s, SUSTAIN 10: full sustain, so the decay does nothing.
- RELEASE 2.4 s: about two seconds to fade out after you let go.
- Listen for: soft entries and long tails, with the vowel still drifting.

context.mod.lfoAmt: In this sound: how wide the vowel movement is.

context.mix.oscB: In this sound: the steady body under the moving vowel.
context.filter.res: In this sound: a slight peak that makes the tone more vocal.

The whole vowel range moves up: a brighter, "eh" and "ee" sound.
Only the synced oscillator is left, thinner and more nasal.

sounds.name: Breathing Pad
sounds.ref: In the style of slow ambient pads that swell and fade on their own
sounds.blurb: Hold one note and it swells and fades by itself, about once every three seconds, with the tone shifting as it breathes.
sounds.how: REPEAT makes the LFO fire both envelopes over and over while a key is held. Usually that is used with short envelopes to make a fast stream of notes. Here the LFO is slowed to about one cycle every three seconds and the envelopes are given slow attacks and long releases, so each firing is a slow swell and fade. The same LFO also moves Oscillator A’s pulse width through the modulation matrix, so the tone changes in step with each breath. The Pro-1 can do this because its LFO is also the clock for REPEAT.

steps.title: Saw and pulse, with a detuned saw
steps.why:
Oscillator A with saw and pulse together, and a detuned saw from B for a slow beating.
- Osc A saw and pulse, PULSE WIDTH 5: on the Pro-1 these add together, and the width starts at 50 %. The pulse is the part that will move.
- OCTAVE 2, FREQUENCY 0, SYNC off: plain and in tune.
- Osc B sawtooth only, OCTAVE 2, FREQUENCY +0.1: a few cents sharp, so the swells are never quite the same.
- KYBD on, LO FREQ NORMAL: B plays normally.
- OSC A 8, OSC B 6, NOISE/EXT 0: the saw-and-pulse leads and the detuned saw sits just under it.
- Listen for: a full, bright, slowly beating tone.

steps.title: Slow the LFO right down
steps.why:
The LFO (low-frequency oscillator) is slowed right down. It will be the clock for the breathing, and here it also moves A’s pulse width.
- LFO triangle on, FREQUENCY 2.5 (0.35 Hz): about one cycle every three seconds. This sets the speed of the breathing and of the pulse-width movement. They cannot be set apart.
- AMOUNT LFO 4: how much the tone changes with each breath.
- LFO route DIRECT, To OSC A PW DIR: A’s pulse width listens to the always-on bus.
- Listen for: the tone slowly thickening and thinning every three seconds.

steps.title: Slow envelopes
steps.why:
Slow ADSR (attack, decay, sustain, release) envelopes on filter and volume make each firing a swell and fade.
- Loudness ATTACK 860 ms: how gently each breath swells. Keep it shorter than half an LFO cycle or the swell never reaches the top.
- Loudness DECAY 2.5 s, RELEASE 2.4 s: with SUSTAIN 8, these set how far each breath fades before the next. Longer and the note never quite goes away.
- CUTOFF 4.5 (about 450 Hz): with RESONANCE 1 and KEYBOARD AMOUNT 6, a dark resting tone.
- ENVELOPE AMOUNT 2.5, filter ATTACK 860 ms: with DECAY 2.5 s, SUSTAIN 6 and RELEASE 2.4 s, the filter opens a little with each swell.
- Listen for: one held note swells in and stays.

steps.title: Switch REPEAT on
steps.why:
REPEAT makes the LFO fire both envelopes over and over while a key is held. The Pro-1 can do this because its LFO is also the clock for REPEAT.
- Repeat on: the LFO opens the envelopes for half of each cycle and lets them go for the other half.
- Drone off: the gate is not held open, so REPEAT can open and close it.
- Listen for: hold one key. The note swells and fades by itself about once every three seconds, with the tone shifting in step.

context.mode.repeat: In this sound: turns the slow LFO into a gate that fires both envelopes about once every three seconds.
context.lfo.rate: In this sound: the speed of the breathing, and of the pulse-width movement too. They cannot be set apart.
context.aenv.attack: In this sound: how gently each breath swells. Keep it shorter than half an LFO cycle or the swell never reaches the top.
context.aenv.release: In this sound: how far each breath fades before the next one. Longer and the note never quite goes away.
context.mod.lfoAmt: In this sound: how much the tone changes with each breath.
context.oscB.freq: In this sound: a slight detune, so the swells are never quite the same.

The note never fades out between swells, so it becomes a pad with a slow pulse in it.
An ordinary slow pad: it swells once and stays.

sounds.name: Twanging Sync Pluck
sounds.ref: In the style of a koto or a plucked zither
sounds.blurb: A soft plucked string with a quick twang at the front of each note.
sounds.how: A plucked string is brightest for a split second and the overtones fall away quickly. Here Oscillator A is synced to Oscillator B, so B holds the pitch steady. The filter envelope is sent to A’s frequency through the modulation matrix, which on a synced oscillator changes the tone, not the pitch: each note starts with A pushed up by nearly an octave and it falls back in about a third of a second. You hear that as a twang, like a string pulled hard and let go, and the note stays in tune throughout.

steps.title: Sync A to B
steps.why:
Sync (hard sync) makes Oscillator A restart every time Oscillator B completes a cycle, so B holds the pitch steady and A’s tuning only changes the tone. On the Pro-1 it is A that follows B.
- Osc A sawtooth, OCTAVE 2, Sync on: the part that will twang, FREQUENCY at 0.
- Osc B triangle only, OCTAVE 2, FREQUENCY 0: sets the pitch. KYBD on, LO FREQ NORMAL.
- OSC A 7, OSC B 3, NOISE/EXT 0: a soft triangle under the synced saw for body.
- Listen for: a plain saw tone for now. With both at the same pitch the sync makes no audible difference until A is moved.

steps.title: Filter envelope to A’s frequency
steps.why:
The filter envelope (ADSR: attack, decay, sustain, release) is sent to Oscillator A’s pitch. Because A is synced, this changes the tone, not the pitch.
- AMOUNT FIL ENV 7: pushes A up by nearly an octave at the start of each note. This is how hard the twang is; at 0 you get a plain saw pluck.
- FIL ENV route DIRECT, To OSC A FREQ DIR: the envelope on the always-on bus, A’s pitch listening.
- ATTACK 2 ms, DECAY 350 ms, SUSTAIN 0: up at once, back down in about a third of a second. This is the length of the twang.
- RELEASE 480 ms: how the envelope finishes after you let go.
- Listen for: each note starts with a bright, vocal “twang” and settles, while staying in tune. Switch SYNC off and each note swoops down in pitch instead.

steps.title: A plucked filter
steps.why:
The filter gives the pluck its brightness at the start.
- CUTOFF 6 (about 1.3 kHz), RESONANCE 0: takes the harsh top off the synced saw.
- KEYBOARD AMOUNT 7: higher notes open the filter most of the way with them.
- ENVELOPE AMOUNT 2: the same envelope opens the filter a little more at the start of each note, adding to the bright front.
- Listen for: a softer tone overall, with the twang still clear at the front.

steps.title: A plucked fade
steps.why:
The loudness envelope turns each note into a plucked string that dies away.
- ATTACK 2 ms: instant, like a pluck.
- DECAY 1.6 s, SUSTAIN 0: about a second and a half to fade to silence even while held. This is how long each string rings.
- RELEASE 920 ms: if you let go early the note still rings on a little.
- Retrigger on: RETRIG restarts both envelopes on every key, so every note gets its own twang.
- Listen for: plucked notes with a quick twang, in the style of a koto.

context.mod.envAmt: In this sound: how hard the twang is. At 0 you get a plain saw pluck.
context.fenv.decay: In this sound: the length of the twang.
context.oscA.sync: In this sound: keeps the pitch steady while the envelope moves Oscillator A. Switch it off and each note swoops down in pitch instead.
context.mix.oscB: In this sound: a soft triangle under the synced saw for body.
context.aenv.decay: In this sound: how long each string rings.

tweaks.hear: A harder, more metallic twang, like a steel string.
The twang becomes a slower "yow" at the start of each note.
Short, dry plucks, like a muted string.

sounds.name: Tight Nasal Loop Riff
sounds.ref: In the style of Daft Punk — "Technologic"
sounds.blurb: Short, pinched riff notes that repeat in a tight loop under a vocal.
sounds.how: Oscillator A plays a narrow pulse, which is thin and nasal on its own. Oscillator B adds a saw, tuned a hair sharp, for a little body. The filter has a resonant peak that stays at about 1.1 kHz whatever note is played, which gives every note the same pinched "nyah" colour. A short filter envelope and RETRIG give each note a clipped front edge, so a fast repeating line stays tight instead of blurring.

steps.title: A narrow pulse with a saw beside it
steps.why:
A narrow pulse gives the thin, nasal edge; a saw beside it adds a little body.
- Osc A pulse only, PULSE WIDTH 2 (22 %): thin and nasal. Towards 5 the tone turns hollow and round; lower than 1.5 it gets very thin.
- Osc A OCTAVE 2, FREQUENCY 0, SYNC off: the main voice.
- Osc B sawtooth only, OCTAVE 2, FREQUENCY +0.1: a hair sharp, so the two beat slowly.
- OSC A 9, OSC B 5, NOISE/EXT 0: the pulse leads.
- Listen for: play one note with OSC B at 0, then bring it in. The pulse alone is thin and reedy; the saw fills it out without losing the edge.

steps.title: A fixed, resonant peak
steps.why:
The filter puts a resonant peak at a fixed point, so every note has the same pinched “nyah” colour.
- CUTOFF 5.8 (about 1.1 kHz): where the nasal peak sits. Lower sounds more muffled; higher sounds brighter and less pinched.
- RESONANCE 4.5: how strong the peak is.
- KEYBOARD AMOUNT 3: kept low so the peak does not follow the notes. At 10 the colour changes from note to note.
- Listen for: the riff takes on a honky, vocal colour that stays the same as the notes move.

steps.title: A clipped front edge
steps.why:
The filter envelope (ADSR: attack, decay, sustain, release) gives each note a clipped front edge.
- ENVELOPE AMOUNT 3: how far the filter opens for the blip.
- ATTACK 2 ms: instant.
- DECAY 71 ms, SUSTAIN 3: a short, bright blip of about 70 ms, then the tone settles a little above the resting cutoff. Longer decay softens the edge.
- RELEASE 34 ms: closes fast.
- Listen for: a short “nyah” on the front of every note.

steps.title: Short, tidy notes
steps.why:
The loudness envelope makes short, tidy notes so the gaps in the loop stay clear.
- ATTACK 2 ms: instant.
- DECAY 170 ms, SUSTAIN 7: a slight drop after the start to a steady level.
- RELEASE 34 ms: each note stops almost as soon as the key is let go.
- Listen for: a tight, clipped riff with clean gaps.

steps.title: Retrigger every note
steps.why:
RETRIG makes every note in the loop get its own front edge.
- Retrigger on: restarts both envelopes on every key press. Without it, notes that touch would share one envelope and the second would lose its blip.
- Listen for: play the riff with Retrigger off, then on. With it off, joined notes go soft at the front; with it on, every note is equally tight.

context.oscA.pw: In this sound: the nasal edge. Towards 5 the tone turns hollow and round; lower than 1.5 it gets very thin.
context.mix.oscB: In this sound: the saw that gives the thin pulse some body. At 0 the riff is reedier and smaller.
context.oscB.freq: In this sound: a tiny detune so the two oscillators beat slowly against each other.
context.filter.cutoff: In this sound: where the nasal peak sits. Lower sounds more muffled; higher sounds brighter and less pinched.
context.filter.res: In this sound: how strong the nasal peak is.
context.filter.kbd: In this sound: kept low so the peak does not follow the notes. At 10 the colour changes from note to note.
context.fenv.decay: In this sound: the length of the blip at the start of each note.
context.mode.retrig: In this sound: gives every note in the loop its own front edge.

tweaks.try: Move between 5 and 6.8 while the riff plays
tweaks.hear: From a closed, "oo"-like riff to a bright, pinched "ee".

tweaks.try: Switch REPEAT on, set LFO FREQUENCY to about 7.8 and hold one key
tweaks.hear: The LFO re-fires the envelopes about eight times a second, so one held key stutters out a stream of short notes.
The pulse becomes a square wave and the riff loses its nasal edge.

sounds.name: Round Bouncing Bass
sounds.ref: In the style of Kraftwerk — "Tour de France"
sounds.blurb: Round, springy bass whose octave jumps bounce up with a quick slide.
sounds.how: A square wave and a triangle an octave below give a round, hollow bass with little buzz. The filter sits low and a short envelope with no sustain opens it a little on every note, then closes it again: that is the bounce. AUTO glide adds a quick slide only when a new note starts before the last one has been let go, so the riff chooses which octave jumps spring up and which land cleanly.

steps.title: Square on top, triangle underneath
steps.why:
A square on top and a triangle an octave below make a round, hollow bass with little buzz.
- Osc A pulse, WIDTH 5, OCTAVE 1: a 50 % square wave, hollow and round. Move the width away from 5 and the bass turns nasal.
- Osc B triangle only, OCTAVE 0: an octave below, a soft low octave that gives weight without adding buzz.
- FREQUENCY 0 on both, SYNC off: in tune, with KYBD on and NORMAL, and following the keys.
- OSC A 8, OSC B 8, NOISE/EXT 0: equal levels.
- Listen for: a full, hollow bass that is still bright on top, because the filter is open.

steps.title: A low filter
steps.why:
The filter sits low so the bass stays round.
- CUTOFF 3.2 (about 180 Hz): leaves a soft, rounded thump. Above about 4.5 it turns buzzy.
- RESONANCE 2.5: a little boost at the cutoff, ready to give the bounce some spring.
- KEYBOARD AMOUNT 6: the higher notes of the riff come through a bit brighter.
- Listen for: a dull, round thump with no front to it yet.

steps.title: Open and close on every note
steps.why:
The filter envelope (ADSR: attack, decay, sustain, release) opens the filter a little on every note and always closes it again. That is the bounce.
- ENVELOPE AMOUNT 4.5: the size of the “bup” at the start of each note.
- ATTACK 2 ms: opens at once.
- DECAY 110 ms, SUSTAIN 0: about a tenth of a second back down, and fully closed however long the key is held. Shorter is tighter; longer turns it into a “wow”.
- RELEASE 34 ms: closes quickly after you let go.
- Listen for: a springy “bup” on each note. Sweep DECAY while the riff plays to hear the bounce tighten and loosen.

steps.title: A short, rounded tail
steps.why:
The loudness envelope gives a short, rounded tail so notes are springy and do not drone.
- ATTACK 2 ms: instant.
- DECAY 270 ms, SUSTAIN 4: the level drops to less than half over about a quarter of a second while the key is held.
- RELEASE 34 ms: notes stop quickly.
- Listen for: bouncy, separate notes. Raise SUSTAIN to 10 to hear the held notes drone.

steps.title: AUTO glide and RETRIG
steps.why:
AUTO glide adds a quick slide only between overlapping notes, so the riff chooses which octave jumps spring up.
- RATE 1.8 (97 ms): a slide of about 100 ms, the length of the slide on the octave jumps.
- Glide mode AUTO: slides only when a new note starts before the last is let go. In the riff the note before each jump up an octave is held just long enough to overlap.
- Retrigger on: keeps the “bup” on every note, slid or not.
- Listen for: the octave jumps spring up with a quick slide, while the other notes land cleanly, in the style of Kraftwerk’s cycling bass.

context.oscA.pw: In this sound: at 5 the pulse is a square wave, which is hollow and round. Move it away from 5 and the bass turns nasal.
context.mix.oscB: In this sound: the triangle an octave down. It gives the weight without adding buzz.
context.filter.cutoff: In this sound: kept low so the bass stays round. Above about 4.5 it turns buzzy.
context.filter.env: In this sound: the size of the "bup" at the start of each note.
context.fenv.decay: In this sound: the length of the bounce. Shorter is tighter; longer turns it into a "wow".
context.fenv.sustain: In this sound: at 0, so the filter closes again on long notes.
context.glide.mode: In this sound: AUTO, so only overlapping notes slide.
context.glide.rate: In this sound: the length of the slide on the octave jumps.

tweaks.hear: Every note now slides into the next, and the bass turns from bouncy to rubbery.
From a dry click on each note to a longer "bwow".
The bounce gets a whistling edge and the bass sounds more electronic.

sounds.name: Squiggly Lead with a Pitch Dip
sounds.ref: In the style of Bernie Worrell — "(Not Just) Knee Deep"
sounds.blurb: Playful, whistling funk lead that drops into each new note and slides between overlapping ones.
sounds.how: Two things give the lead its squiggle. The filter envelope is also sent to the pitch of both oscillators through the DIRECT bus, so every detached note starts about two semitones sharp and falls into tune in a third of a second, while a resonant filter sweeps shut at the same time. AUTO glide then slides between notes that overlap, and because RETRIG is off those notes skip the dip, so the line alternates between dipping attacks and smooth slides. The filter envelope has no sustain, so the pitch always settles exactly in tune.

steps.title: Saw and a slightly detuned square
steps.why:
A saw and a slightly detuned square make a lead that sounds wider than one oscillator.
- Osc A sawtooth only, OCTAVE 2, FREQUENCY 0: the bright main voice.
- Osc B pulse only, PULSE WIDTH 5 (50 %): a square, hollow, under the saw.
- Osc B OCTAVE 2, FREQUENCY +0.1: a hair sharp, so the pair beat slowly.
- SYNC off, KYBD on, LO FREQ NORMAL: both free and following the keys.
- OSC A 8, OSC B 5, NOISE/EXT 0: the saw in front, the square tucked under it.
- Listen for: a bright, slightly moving tone.

steps.title: A resonant filter that whistles as it closes
steps.why:
A resonant filter that whistles as it closes gives each note a short “yow”.
- CUTOFF 5.2 (about 730 Hz): the resting point the filter falls back to.
- RESONANCE 6: a strong peak. It makes the closing filter whistle. Below about 4 the lead is just bright and plain.
- KEYBOARD AMOUNT 7: the filter follows the line most of the way.
- ENVELOPE AMOUNT 4.5, ATTACK 15 ms: the filter envelope (ADSR: attack, decay, sustain, release) opens the filter quickly with a soft front, not a click.
- DECAY 300 ms, SUSTAIN 0, RELEASE 87 ms: it closes over about a third of a second and stays shut.
- Listen for: a vocal “yow” on each note.

steps.title: Send the filter envelope to pitch
steps.why:
The same filter envelope is sent to the pitch of both oscillators, so each detached note starts sharp and dips into tune.
- AMOUNT FIL ENV 2.8: about two semitones of dip. It is the part that makes the lead sound playful.
- FIL ENV route DIRECT: on the always-on bus, which carries only the filter envelope here.
- To OSC A FREQ DIR, To OSC B FREQ DIR: both oscillators dip together and stay in tune with each other.
- Listen for: each note dropping into place over a third of a second. SUSTAIN at 0 in the last step matters: raise it and held notes stay sharp.

steps.title: Lead volume
steps.why:
The loudness envelope keeps fast notes separate.
- ATTACK 2 ms: instant.
- DECAY 170 ms, SUSTAIN 8: a small drop to a high held level.
- RELEASE 87 ms: short, so fast notes do not smear.
- VOLUME 8: makes up for the level the resonance takes away.
- Listen for: punchy, separate notes, each with its dip and “yow”.

steps.title: AUTO glide, RETRIG off
steps.why:
AUTO glide with RETRIG off gives the line its mix of dipping attacks and smooth slides.
- RATE 3 (270 ms): a slide of about a quarter of a second.
- Glide mode AUTO: only overlapping notes slide.
- Retrigger off: overlapped notes do not restart the envelopes, so they slide without a dip.
- Listen for: in the riff the second note runs into the third and the sixth into the seventh. Those slide smoothly with no dip, while the detached notes dip, in the style of Bernie Worrell’s squiggly leads.

context.mod.envAmt: The depth of the pitch dip: 2.8 is about two semitones. It is also the part that makes the lead sound playful.
context.mod.toAFreq: At DIR, so Oscillator A’s pitch follows the DIRECT bus, which carries only the filter envelope.
context.mod.toBFreq: At DIR as well, so both oscillators dip together and stay in tune with each other.
context.fenv.sustain: At 0, so the pitch always comes back to the note. Raise it and held notes stay sharp.
context.fenv.decay: How long the dip and the filter sweep take to settle.
context.fenv.attack: About 15 ms, so the dip and the "yow" have a soft front and not a click.
context.filter.res: Makes the closing filter whistle. Below about 4 the lead is just bright and plain.
context.mode.retrig: Off, so overlapped notes do not restart the envelope and slide without a dip.

tweaks.hear: At 0 it is a plain resonant lead. At 4.5 each note swoops down about five semitones and sounds like a cartoon.
From a quick flick into each note to a slow, sagging fall.
Every note dips, including the slid ones, and the line gets busier and less smooth.

sounds.name: Slow Open-Fifth Swell
sounds.ref: In the style of Brian Eno — "Becalmed" (Another Green World)
sounds.blurb: Soft, still tone that fades in slowly on each note, with a quiet fifth above it and a slow shimmer in the pulse.
sounds.how: The Pro-1 plays one note at a time, so the second oscillator is tuned a fifth above the first to make every note an open interval. Both follow the keys, so the fifth moves with the melody. A slow volume attack of nearly a second and a release of about three seconds take away any sense of a key being struck. A very slow LFO moves the width of the pulse, which keeps the tone changing gently while it holds. A low filter with little resonance keeps it dark and calm.

steps.title: A square wave and a triangle a fifth above
steps.why:
The Pro-1 plays one note at a time, so Oscillator B is tuned a fifth above A to make every note an open interval.
- Osc A pulse, WIDTH 5, OCTAVE 2: a 50 % square, hollow and plain.
- Osc B triangle, FREQUENCY 5 (+7 st): at OCTAVE 2, exactly seven semitones up, a fifth above.
- KYBD on, LO FREQ NORMAL, SYNC off: both follow the keys, so the fifth moves with the melody.
- OSC A 7, OSC B 6, NOISE/EXT 0: the fifth a little quieter. Lower it until you only just hear it for a plainer tone.
- Listen for: two pitches from one key, the note and the fifth above it.

steps.title: A dark, quiet filter
steps.why:
A dark, quiet filter keeps the tone calm.
- CUTOFF 4 (about 320 Hz): dark. Raise it and the tone gets closer to a reed organ.
- RESONANCE 1: very little peak.
- KEYBOARD AMOUNT 7: higher notes are not much brighter than low ones.
- ENVELOPE AMOUNT 1.5, filter ATTACK 860 ms: with DECAY 1.0 s, SUSTAIN 5 and RELEASE 2.4 s, a small, slow filter envelope (ADSR: attack, decay, sustain, release) that opens the tone a little as each note fades in.
- Listen for: a soft, muted interval.

steps.title: Fade in and fade out
steps.why:
The loudness envelope takes away any sense of a key being struck.
- ATTACK 860 ms: nearly a second, so no note starts with an edge.
- DECAY 170 ms, SUSTAIN 10: full sustain, so the decay does nothing.
- RELEASE 3.1 s: about three seconds, so each note fades under the next.
- Retrigger off, glide RATE 0: no legato tricks and no slide; notes simply fade in and out.
- Listen for: notes that come in without an edge and hang on after you let go.

steps.title: Slow pulse-width movement
steps.why:
A very slow LFO (low-frequency oscillator) moves the pulse width, known as PWM (pulse width modulation), so the held tone keeps changing gently.
- LFO triangle on, FREQUENCY 2.5 (0.35 Hz): one cycle about every three seconds. The speed of the shimmer.
- AMOUNT LFO 6: how far the width moves. More gives a stronger shimmer.
- LFO route DIRECT, To OSC A PW DIR: A’s pulse width always follows the slow LFO.
- Listen for: the square slowly narrows and widens, so the tone changes colour without changing pitch or loudness.

context.oscB.freq: At 5: seven semitones, a fifth above Oscillator A. This is what makes one key sound like an open interval.
context.mix.oscB: The level of the fifth. Lower it until you only just hear it for a plainer tone.
context.aenv.attack: Nearly a second, so no note starts with an edge.
context.aenv.release: About three seconds: each note fades under the next one.
context.mod.lfoAmt: How far the pulse width moves. More gives a stronger shimmer.
context.mod.toAPw: At DIR, so the slow LFO always moves Oscillator A’s pulse width.
context.lfo.rate: The speed of the shimmer, about one cycle every three seconds.
context.filter.cutoff: Keeps the sound dark. Raise it and the tone gets closer to a reed organ.

tweaks.hear: The interval becomes a fourth, five semitones, which sounds more open and less settled.
At 5 the notes arrive almost at once; at 8.5 each takes about two seconds to arrive and the melody blurs.
The pulse narrows to about a fifth of its cycle at each end of the swing and the tone thins out and fills in again.

sounds.name: Steel-Style Swell and Bend
sounds.ref: In the style of Daniel Lanois — "Still Water" (Acadie)
sounds.blurb: Warm, soft tone that swells in without a pick attack and bends up into notes like a pedal steel.
sounds.how: Daniel Lanois is known for pedal steel guitar played with slow volume swells. This patch copies those two moves. A volume attack of about half a second hides the start of each note, the way a steel player brings the volume pedal up after picking. AUTO glide with RETRIG off does the bend: when you press a new key while holding the last one, the pitch slides up to it inside the same swell, with no new attack. A triangle under a quiet saw keeps the tone warm, and vibrato waits on the mod wheel.

steps.title: A triangle with a little saw
steps.why:
A triangle with a little saw gives a warm tone with a string-like edge.
- Osc B triangle only, OCTAVE 2, FREQUENCY 0: carries most of the sound, soft and round.
- Osc A sawtooth only, OCTAVE 2, FREQUENCY −0.1: a hair flat against the triangle, for a slow, gentle beat.
- SYNC off, KYBD on, LO FREQ NORMAL: both free and following the keys.
- OSC A 5, OSC B 9, NOISE/EXT 0: the saw adds the edge of a string. Turn it down for a rounder, flute-like tone.
- Listen for: a warm tone with a slow beat and a slight edge.

steps.title: Warm filter that opens with the swell
steps.why:
A warm filter that opens with the swell.
- CUTOFF 4.8 (about 550 Hz): warm and fairly dark.
- RESONANCE 2: a slight peak.
- KEYBOARD AMOUNT 6: higher notes brighten a little with the line.
- ENVELOPE AMOUNT 1.5, filter ATTACK 570 ms: with DECAY 1.0 s, SUSTAIN 6 and RELEASE 1.5 s, a slow filter envelope (ADSR: attack, decay, sustain, release) so the tone brightens slightly as the volume rises.
- Listen for: notes that open a little in the first half second.

steps.title: The volume swell
steps.why:
The volume swell hides the start of each note, the way a steel player brings the volume pedal up after picking.
- ATTACK 570 ms: just over half a second. At 0 you hear a hard start; at 7 each note fades up.
- DECAY 420 ms, SUSTAIN 9: a small dip to a nearly full held level.
- RELEASE 1.5 s: notes ring for about a second and a half after you let go.
- Listen for: no pick sound. Each detached note fades up out of nothing.

steps.title: Bends with AUTO glide
steps.why:
AUTO glide with RETRIG off does the bend: a new key pressed while the last is held slides up inside the same swell.
- RATE 3.5 (370 ms): a slide of about 0.4 s, the speed of the bend.
- Glide mode AUTO: only overlapping notes bend. Detached notes start fresh.
- Retrigger off: a bent note stays inside the same swell instead of fading in again.
- Listen for: in the riff the first note is held into the second, so it bends up a whole tone. The same happens later going up to the A, and down at the end.

steps.title: Vibrato on the mod wheel
steps.why:
The LFO (low-frequency oscillator, a slow wave for moving other controls) adds vibrato on the mod wheel only.
- LFO triangle on, FREQUENCY 6.5 (3.8 Hz): a smooth, fairly slow vibrato, about four a second.
- AMOUNT LFO 1.8: the most vibrato the wheel can bring in, about three quarters of a semitone each way.
- LFO route WHEEL: nothing changes until you push the wheel.
- To OSC A FREQ WH, To OSC B FREQ WH: both pitches listen to the WHEEL bus and move together.
- Listen for: add it on the long notes after a bend, as a steel player would with the bar.

context.aenv.attack: The swell. At 0 you hear a hard start; at 7 each note fades up.
context.aenv.release: How long a note rings after you let go.
context.glide.mode: AUTO: only overlapping notes bend. Detached notes start fresh.
context.mode.retrig: Off, so a bent note stays inside the same swell instead of fading in again.
context.mix.oscA: The saw adds the edge of a string. Turn it down for a rounder, flute-like tone.
context.oscA.freq: A hair flat against the triangle, for a slow, gentle beat.
context.mod.lfoAmt: The most vibrato the wheel can bring in.
context.mod.lfoRoute: WHEEL, so vibrato is only there when you push the mod wheel.

tweaks.hear: From a quick flick up to the note to a slow, sighing bend.
At 5 the swell is short and you hear the start of the note; at 8 it takes over a second and sounds like a volume pedal pushed slowly.
Each bent note fades in again from nothing, so the bend is lost under the swell.
